The Tether connection is both asset and liability — distribution relationships and brand recognition offset by the regulatory scrutiny that follows Tether everywhere. Whether Malta's MFSA carries the same weight as France's ACPR in the MiCA credibility hierarchy is no longer an abstract question — the answer is being written in the enforcement file.

usdr-stablr.title: One Key From Compliant
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR holds a Malta MFSA EMI license under MiCA with 100% reserves in cash and short-term government bonds, reviewed quarterly by Grant Thornton — a regulatory stack including formal {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} that checks every European compliance box while the market barely notices at single-digit-millions in supply. Then May 2026 rewrote the story: an attacker compromised StablR's 1-of-3 minting multisig and printed $13.5 million of unbacked USDR and EURR, the quote broke violently below par, and the issuer froze minting and redemption while disclosing to Malta's MFSA that circulating supply was no longer fully 1:1 backed — MiCA's cardinal sin, committed by a MiCA poster child. Weeks later the report card reads F with the primary market still suspended, and the thin single-pool Ethereum footprint that once merely embarrassed the liquidity score now defines the only exit anyone has. With liquidity that shallow, any meaningful exit runs through StablR's own issuer API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route rather than the order book. Europe's MiCA framework was supposed to be the catalyst for regulated stablecoins; USDR is now the test of what the framework does after the incident report is filed.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}}-backed stablecoin distributing yield daily, with Bermuda DABA licensing and Chainlink PoR — elegant for retail but awkward for DeFi. OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing stablecoin fixed at $1 that distributes T-bill yield daily by increasing holder balances — backed 70% by OpenEden's own TBILL tokens, 15% by BlackRock BUIDL, 5% by Franklin Templeton BENJI, and 10% in USDC as a cash buffer. The Bermuda BMA DABA license and Chainlink Proof of Reserves provide regulatory and transparency layers that most rebasing stablecoins lack, with on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} of the underlying {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} basket, though the peg score of 81 and 44 depeg events — including one that spiked nearly 17,000 basis points above peg — reveal the mechanical challenge of maintaining a $1 price on a token whose supply changes daily. The backstop scores a modest 52 with capacity issues, reflecting the illiquidity gap between holding tokenized treasuries and providing instant dollar {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}}. Deployed across four chains, USDO is elegant for retail but awkward for DeFi protocols that don't handle rebasing tokens — hence the cUSDO wrapper for composability.

usda-anzens.title: Cardano's Lonely Dollar
usda-anzens.text: Cardano's only MSB-licensed dollar pairs clean BitGo-custodied reserves with one of the worst peg records on Pharos, dragged down by absent DeFi depth. Anzens USDA offers the cleanest backing on Cardano — 60% USD cash, 40% U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, all {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}-managed by BitGo Trust under a FinCEN MSB license — yet it has logged hundreds of recorded depeg events, with deviations spiking as far as +2558 bps. The problem isn't the backing; it's the chain. A single thin DEX pool and Cardano-only deployment mean there is no meaningful arbitrage infrastructure to enforce the peg, producing a C- safety grade despite reserves that would earn a much higher mark on any chain with real DeFi depth. The only exit is KYC-verified bank transfers through Anzens for {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, with multi-day settlement and no quick on-chain escape hatch. Supply has drained by nearly half over the past month, suggesting holders have reached the same conclusion. USDA is proof that sound reserves are necessary but nowhere near sufficient — you also need a market that can actually trade the thing.

usdf-falcon.title: Ethena's Wilder Cousin
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance takes the {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} playbook and cranks the risk dial: BTC shorts, stablecoins, ETH shorts, tokenized Treasuries, and the part that separates it from Ethena — altcoins like DOGE, FET, TRX, and TON hedged with {{term:perpetual}}perp{{/term}} shorts on centralized exchanges. The live safety profile has softened, and the culprit is plain: the peg mostly behaves, but liquidity is the soft spot and the whitelisted on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path is a bottleneck. The sUSDf yield attracts capital faster than the exotic, altcoin-heavy collateral mix can comfortably support, which is exactly the tension the report card keeps pricing in. Real-time reserve transparency via ht.digital is a genuine differentiator, not a marketing footnote. But a track record of brief sub-peg blips suggests the altcoin hedging strategy stumbles where BTC-only approaches would not. USDf is Ethena's wilder cousin, and the family resemblance is not the risky part.

europ-schuman.title: Credentials Without Scale
europ-schuman.text: EUROP is Schuman Financial's ACPR-licensed euro stablecoin backed by euro cash at EU banks — credentials in abundance, market share negligible. Schuman Financial stacks every credential the euro stablecoin market demands — ACPR EMI license under MiCA, KPMG {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, 98% of reserves in euro cash at Societe Generale and peer EU banks, a 2% buffer beyond par — and still sits at barely 8.6M EUR circulating, roughly the size of a mid-tier DeFi protocol's {{term:treasury}}treasury{{/term}}. That mismatch is now showing up in the score: a B- overall, dragged down by a D on liquidity, says the credentials are no longer enough to lift a token this small out of the second tier. The peg itself is not the worry — it holds an A-grade tightness and rarely strays from the calm end of the stress scale, with dozens of brief sub-par blips and a worst drawdown of 229 bps that read as thin-market noise rather than structural instability. The July 1 MiCA cutover at least thinned the field — EUROP now stands among the eight authorized euro stablecoins in a market that just repriced compliance from credential to prerequisite. The five-chain deployment including XRPL and Plasma is an unusual distribution bet — reaching beyond EVM chains where the established euro competitors have not yet planted flags — but distribution without depth just spreads the same thin float across more order books.

brz-transfero.title: Pegged to Volatility Itself
brz-transfero.text: BRZ is Transfero's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 by KYC'd users against BRL cash held in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at a Brazilian institution — its depeg history is FX volatility, not reserve failure. The dozens of recorded depeg events, including swings approaching 10,000 basis points below peg, are not evidence of product failure but of what happens when you peg a token to the Brazilian real and price it against dollar-denominated markets. The D safety grade is largely a function of that FX-driven peg volatility rather than reserve inadequacy, since BRZ is backed 100% by BRL cash at a Central Bank of Brazil-authorized institution with Swiss VQF registration. The exit story has improved but remains the binding constraint: DEX depth now scores in the C range rather than the basement, yet a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee through Transfero's offchain issuer path still means the cleanest way out of any sizable position is the issuer window, not the secondary market. Deployed across multiple chains with hundreds of millions of reais in circulation, BRZ serves a genuine need in Latin America's largest crypto market — and while it tends to sit at the calm end of the stress scale day to day, thin-by-major-stablecoin-standards liquidity and the underlying FX exposure are a standing reminder that non-USD stablecoins carry risks no reserve structure can hedge away.

rlusd-ripple.title: The Institutional On-Ramp
rlusd-ripple.text: Ripple's NYDFS-supervised dollar is backed by a very-low-risk reserve split across {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}, and cash, with monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} from Deloitte under a New York trust charter. That reserve is the kind of boring institutional machinery a settlement token should have, and RLUSD is very much a settlement token rather than a DeFi primitive. The live grade has eased from the earlier headline because secondary-market depth and concentration still matter even when the collateral is immaculate. Brief depeg events from early price discovery are less a reserve indictment than a reminder that new tokens need time to build market plumbing. DEX liquidity remains concentrated in a handful of pools, consistent with a payments corridor product whose real exit is issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The paperwork keeps compounding: RLUSD launched in Japan as the first stablecoin approved under the Type 4 electronic-payment-instrument regime via SBI, Ripple's Luxembourg entity upgraded to a full MiCA CASP authorization covering the EEA, and Mastercard added RLUSD to its stablecoin settlement stack. RLUSD looks sturdy, but it is sturdy in the way a bank product is sturdy: excellent paperwork, narrow on-chain spontaneity.

feusd-felix.title: Liquity Fork on Hyperliquid
feusd-felix.text: feUSD is a Liquity-v2-fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Hyperliquid, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by HYPE ecosystem tokens — concentrated chain risk, sturdy redemption mechanics. Felix Protocol cloned Liquity V2 onto Hyperliquid's unproven L1 and loaded the CDPs with HYPE and its liquid-staking derivatives — an asset class Pharos rates very-high risk — alongside bridged Bitcoin. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is genuinely strong for a DeFi-native coin, with zero-fee atomic collateral redemption and an interest-rate-sorted queue, and the peg itself has held tight, rarely drifting from the calm end of the stress scale despite a long tail of brief blips. But the C safety grade tells the real story, and it is not about the peg: when your primary collateral is the native token of the chain you live on, a single ecosystem shock hits both your backing and your exit {{term:liquidation}}liquidity simultaneously{{/term}}. That structural fragility shows up as a weak resilience grade and a failing decentralization score — a multisig still holds the admin keys, caps, and pause — which is what drags an otherwise well-pegged coin down to a middling overall mark.

dusd-standx.title: The Quiet Basis Trader
dusd-standx.text: DUSD is StandX's {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar: an Ethena-style {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} through Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with less theater and less public verification. The reserve model is mostly spot-long and {{term:perpetual}}perp-short{{/term}} exposure on BTC, ETH, SOL, and BNB, plus a small stability buffer, so the product lives or dies by CEX operations and hedging discipline. The live grade remains weak because exotic collateral, centralized custody, no published proof of reserves, and an issuer-API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path are not small footnotes. The peg record has looked cleaner than the structure deserves, which suggests the desk knows what it is doing as long as the infrastructure beneath it behaves. The stress panel has moved out of the sleepy framing the old summary used, so the right read is not panic but active monitoring. Trusting a basis trader is one thing; verifying the basis trader is the part StandX still leaves mostly off-chain.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen’s Blockchain Experiment
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EURCV is SG-FORGE's MiCA EUR stablecoin; reserves held in EUR cash at SocGen itself, top institutional safety with thin DEX liquidity. EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of a systemically important European bank, with reserves held 100% in euro cash at Société Générale itself — institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that earns the highest marks available in both resilience and dependency risk. The B safety grade makes EURCV one of the highest-rated euro stablecoins on Pharos, held back primarily by the expected F in decentralization — an inevitable trade-off when a 160-year-old bank decides to issue tokens on public blockchains. The DEWS stress reading is among the lowest on the entire dashboard, suggesting the product is operationally serene despite the thin DEX liquidity that plagues most euro stablecoins. Deployed across Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar, and Solana with MiCA EMI licensing from France’s ACPR, whether EURCV is the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab’s pet project depends on whether SocGen commits distribution resources that match its regulatory credentials. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through SG-FORGE.

yusd-aegis.title: Funding Rate Roulette
yusd-aegis.text:
A delta-neutral BTC-collateralized synthetic dollar with best-in-class proof-of-reserves but a poor C- grade — yield is funding-rate roulette priced into the score.

Aegis YUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} stablecoin built entirely on BTC — spot long at Fireblocks, Copper, and Ceffu under institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} hedged by COIN-M {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts — which means the C- grade is the market's verdict on using an active {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} position as collateral. Dozens of historical depeg events with a worst excursion of +1705 bps tell the story of a token whose peg stability is a function of {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} economics and exchange availability, not reserve quality. Real-time proof-of-reserves through Accountable is genuinely best-in-class transparency — you can watch the positions live, which is more than Ethena offers — but transparency doesn't reduce the underlying risk of CEX custody concentration. The grade sits in poor territory because the funding-rate yield is priced against the scenario where negative rates eat the insurance fund faster than it refills.

reusd-resupply.title: Leverage All the Way Down
reusd-resupply.text:
A CDP coin minted against Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares — recursive yield wrapped in a token, with a 1% redemption-fee floor.

Resupply's reUSD wraps Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares into a dollar token whose collateral is itself earning yield on other stablecoins — turtles of leverage atop a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee floor sourced from a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} architecture. The C- report card and hundreds of recorded depeg events tell the tale of exotic collateral doing exotic things, though supply has stabilized around $35M after a slight contraction from last week's $37M. DEX liquidity is concentrated (HHI 0.59) across just 6 pools with an effective TVL of only $825K, meaning any serious exit would blow through the order book. reUSD tends to camp in the watch end of the stress scale rather than the calm one, and with a yield-to-risk ratio under 0.02 the market correctly prices it as a recursive instrument rather than a stable store of value — you hold this to farm, not to park.

tbill-openeden.title: T-Bills With a Token Wrapper
tbill-openeden.text: A tokenized BVI Treasury fund managed by BNY Investment Management, KYC-gated and trading at NAV above $1 with zero secondary liquidity. OpenEden's TBILL holds short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills as a tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} with institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and its price drifts steadily above its original dollar as accumulated NAV appreciation accrues to holders rather than resetting to par. The B- report card and the spotless depeg record are the signature of a KYC-gated {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund structure that functions as intended: professional investors collect on-chain Treasury yield, and everyone else can look but not touch. That same gating is what drags the grade down — pristine A+ resilience and dependency scores sit next to a D for liquidity and decentralization, because a token with no DEX pools and no permissionless mint is safe by construction but useless to anyone who isn't on the subscriber list. The complete absence of secondary market liquidity is a feature, not a bug — TBILL redeems through the issuer at NAV with multi-day settlement under EY {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-backed reporting, which matches the structure of a regulated BVI fund.

a7a5-old-vector.title: The Sanctioned Dollar's Mirror
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is a centralized ruble stablecoin from Old Vector LLC, backed 1:1 by RUB deposits at sanctioned Russian state bank Promsvyazbank. A7A5 is a ruble-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by deposits at Promsvyazbank — a Russian state-owned bank under Western sanctions — which is why Pharos classifies its {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} as institutional-sanctioned and its reserve risk as very-high despite the collateral being plain fiat currency. Issued by Old Vector LLC under a Kyrgyz VASP license with quarterly audits from an independent Kyrgyz firm, the regulatory architecture is technically compliant with its home jurisdiction while being functionally untouchable by Western financial infrastructure. Since 2026-02-09 the issuer has passed through nearly all of the reserve yield to holders as additional A7A5 at the CBR key rate minus one percentage point — a step up from the previous 50% split that makes A7A5 one of the few {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoins whose holders directly capture a sanctioned bank's deposit rate. Since spring the net has only widened: the EU's 20th sanctions package extended the ban beyond the token to the exchanges and payment agents distributing it, Moscow retaliated by sanctioning a British teenage researcher who documented A7A5's war-finance flows, and blockchain-analytics firms now dispute the issuer's headline volumes — attributing roughly a third to wash trading and noting activity collapsed after the Grinex shutdown. Whether A7A5 represents financial innovation for an isolated economy or sanctions evasion with a token wrapper depends entirely on whose compliance framework you're applying.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: The Presidential Stablecoin
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 is politically loud and structurally boring, which is exactly the joke. Under the Trump-affiliated wrapper sits a BitGo Trust-issued dollar backed by short-term Treasuries, government money-market funds, and cash deposits under a South Dakota trust charter with recurring attestations. The product risk is not exotic collateral; it is centralized issuer control, role-gated minting, issuer-only redemption, and whether the brand helps distribution or narrows the buyer pool to people already nodding. Pharos therefore reads USD1 as a conventional regulated stablecoin wearing a campaign hat, not a new monetary primitive. The reserves are the least dramatic part, which may be the most damning thing one can say about the launch.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Institutional Backing, Amateur Plumbing
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX has 80% T-bills and 20% cash at global tier-1 banks under a Hong Kong TCSP license, which makes its D safety grade a case study in how clean reserves mean nothing without functional market infrastructure. Supply sits across three chains (Ethereum, Flare, Songbird), but the single DEX pool holding the float with a few hundred dollars in effective TVL is not a liquidity profile — it's a rounding error, and the F liquidity grade says as much. Hundreds of recorded depeg events and a worst deviation past 7,000 basis points tell the story of a stablecoin that periodically trades around 28 cents on the dollar despite holding Treasuries at par. The stress engine reads USDX as sitting at the calm end of the scale, but that placidity is itself the tell: there is no two-sided market thrashing the price back, so nothing registers as stress. {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} from a Hong Kong TCSP-licensed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} provider and 270+ institutional clients haven't translated into the on-chain arbitrage loops that keep prices honest, and same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} cannot substitute for the missing secondary market — leaving USDX as expensive proof that custodial credibility and stablecoin stability are entirely different problems.

pusd-plume.title: USDC With a Detour
pusd-plume.text:
A USDC wrapper that routes through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC checks — extra trust layers on top of an asset that was already perfectly functional.

Plume's pUSD takes USDC, routes it through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC compliance checks, and issues a wrapped token on Ethereum and Plume Chain — adding smart contract risk, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} abstraction, and a new trust layer to an asset that was already perfectly functional. The safety grade has sunk to a D on a failing liquidity mark, and while zero-fee same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} suggests the wrapper functions, the deviation history — a dozen-plus blips capped by a catastrophic 4,049-basis-point negative excursion — records at least one moment when it emphatically did not. Supply idles in the single-digit millions with on-chain depth confined to a single thin pool, raising the question of whether the RWAfi ecosystem narrative generates enough demand to justify the wrapper's existence. pUSD remains a solution in search of a problem that Plume hasn't yet proven it has.

bold-liquity.title: Immutable Code, Perfect Scores
bold-liquity.text: BOLD is Liquity V2's decentralized dollar stablecoin, minted from immutable {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults against WETH, wstETH, and rETH only — no governance keys, no admin functions, no RWA exposure. Liquity V2's BOLD remains the highest-rated DeFi stablecoin on the dashboard, with an A+ profile that looks structural rather than lucky. Backed by wstETH, WETH, and rETH in immutable contracts, BOLD achieves what most decentralized stablecoins only aspire to: genuine peg stability alongside genuine decentralization. The high-quality {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop with permissionless atomic collateral redemption at 50 bps provides one of DeFi's hardest peg floors, while user-set interest rates and Stability Pool yield create self-correcting incentives that keep BOLD close to par. Supply is growing across seven chains, but the total remains small relative to the design's ambition — proof that the market still prices convenience and composability above architectural purity.

avusd-avant.title: Avalanche's Quiet Contender
avusd-avant.text: avUSD is Avant's centralized dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for USDC and deployed into actively managed {{term:delta-neutral}}market-neutral{{/term}} strategies for yield — avUSD itself does not accrue yield, the staked savUSD does. Avant's avUSD is a USDC-backed base token for the Avant protocol, with deposited USDC routed into 0xPartners-managed market-neutral strategies and protected by a loss-absorption reserve. The token itself does not accrue yield: users stake avUSD into the separately tracked savUSD senior tranche when they want yield exposure, while avUSD remains the redeemable receipt for USDC exits at a 5-basis-point fee and one-to-seven-day settlement window. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and BVI domicile mean trust runs through Avant's operational integrity rather than a regulatory framework, which is why the backstop {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} remains queue-based rather than a hard on-chain par floor. Five recorded depegs, including one at 321 basis points below peg, show the market can still stress the wrapper even when the current peg score is high.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text:
The only stablecoin registered under the 1933 and 1940 Acts — SOFR-minus-50bps via a face-amount certificate, with full KYC and zero DeFi composability as the price of legitimacy.

YLDS is that rarest of crypto products: a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing stablecoin{{/term}} registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940, paying SOFR minus 50 basis points through a fixed face-amount certificate structure that the SEC has explicitly blessed. The reserves are 86% overnight {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} repos and 13% {{term:money-market-fund}}money market funds{{/term}} at UMB Bank, KPMG-audited, with institutional-top custody — a {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} reserve stack so conservative it makes Circle look adventurous. Deployed on Solana and Provenance rather than Ethereum, YLDS targets a distribution path through Figure's existing lending platform rather than DeFi composability. The trade-off is clear: full SEC registration means mandatory KYC, restricted transferability, and zero DeFi integration, but for institutions that need a yield product whose legal status doesn't require a creative memo from outside counsel, YLDS is the only game in town.

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ is DNB-supervised under MiCAR at 102% overcollateralization with EU/US sovereign bonds and Tier-1 bank deposits — perfect peg score, modest distribution. Quantoz's USDQ holds the distinction of being supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank under MiCAR with reserves maintained at 102% overcollateralization — 69% in Netherlands, German, and U.S. government bonds with 31% in cash at Tier 1 European banks, all held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. A perfect peg score of 100 with zero depeg events and zero {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fees makes USDQ the cleanest-performing USD stablecoin outside the top ten by every stability metric Pharos tracks. Deployed across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand, the distribution is modest but the regulatory positioning is unmatched: DNB supervision, MiCAR compliance, regulatory {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and a Visa principal membership for stablecoin-linked debit cards turn compliance into competitive advantage. Whether the Dutch compliance premium translates into adoption at scale depends on whether European crypto users value regulatory certainty enough to choose USDQ over the familiar convenience of USDC.

usdn-noble.title: The Transit Dollar
usdn-noble.text: Noble's USDN is a rebasing dollar backed by M0's short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} structure, with collateral maintained by M0 minters and verified through on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. That is a far more conventional reserve story than its Cosmos-native wrapper suggests: holders receive the accumulated T-bill yield while the protocol tracks their principal against M0's rebasing multiplier. The problem is not that the collateral reads like a casino chip; it is that USDN needs demand, usable exits, and confidence in a layered bridge-and-minter arrangement. A stable peg can coexist with a very small market, because quiet is not the same thing as liquid. USDN is credible infrastructure looking for a reason not to be merely transit capital.

usdu-unitas.title: The JLP Hedge Fund
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas's USDu routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens hedged by CEX perpetual shorts through Copper and Ceffu, a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} dressed up as a stablecoin. Unitas routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens — a basket of BTC, ETH, SOL, and USDC earning Jupiter Perps trading fees — while hedging the spot exposure with CEX {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} settlement. The remaining 20% sits as margin for the short positions, making the entire reserve an active trading strategy with exotic collateral quality classification and zero idle assets. Singapore-domiciled with Accountable providing real-time zero-knowledge solvency proofs, USDu's transparency is a genuine upgrade over the 'trust us' school of yield products. Deployed on BSC and Solana with a peg score of 99 and only six depeg events, the machinery works — but the 80% dependency on USDC means every dollar of backing passes through Circle before reaching Jupiter's perps market, adding a layer of counterparty risk the hedge fund framing might obscure.

mnee-mnee.title: BSV Refugee, T-Bill Convert
mnee-mnee.text: Fiat-backed USD stablecoin with pristine T-bill plus cash reserves and Wolf and Company attestations, dragged down to a C+ by Antigua licensing, institutional-unregulated custody, and near-zero on-chain liquidity. MNEE wraps 85% short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} and 15% cash into a clean reserve profile attested by Wolf and Company — the kind of composition that earns an A+ dependency score and a peg score of 97. The C+ safety grade is a product of infrastructure, not reserves: Antigua FSRC licensing, institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a single Ethereum deployment with effectively no usable DEX depth leave holders dependent on issuer-API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} as the only credible exit. A handful of depeg events, including one plunge past 600 basis points, expose what happens when a nine-figure stablecoin has no on-chain arbitrage infrastructure to defend parity. Lately the plumbing has thinned further: listed venues have gone quiet enough that Pharos currently has no usable price feed for the token, and supply has drifted down double digits — for a coin whose only credible exit was already the issuer API, dark price discovery is not a detail. MNEE proved a fiat-backed coin can have pristine reserves and still score like a mid-tier product when the plumbing around it is this thin.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's Singapore Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: Paxos's USDG is the Singapore sequel under MAS supervision, with all-very-low-risk reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered and a dual-jurisdiction MiCA EU issuance no competitor matches. After Binance's BUSD died under regulatory fire, Paxos relocated its stablecoin ambitions to Singapore, where USDG now sits under a MAS Major Payment Institution license with reserves split between DBS Bank and Standard Chartered — institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that matches Circle and exceeds Tether. The all-very-low-risk reserve composition and A resilience grade make USDG structurally one of the safest stablecoins in existence, which makes the lowest peg score among rated top-ten coins a curious anomaly — a brief tracking history with early growing pains rather than structural fragility. The zero-fee {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and additional EU issuance via a MiCA-compliant Finnish entity give USDG a dual-jurisdiction strategy that no competitor currently matches. The pedigree now includes card rails: Mastercard's June settlement expansion put USDG — alongside its Paxos siblings PYUSD and USDP — into the set of regulated stablecoins eligible to settle card obligations across its network. The catch is on-chain presence: concentrated on just a few chains with modest DEX depth, USDG's institutional pedigree still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Southeast Asia's FX Shortcut
xsgd-straitsx.text:
A MAS-licensed SGD stablecoin with DBS/StanChart reserves and twice-monthly attestations, now grading A- on real Southeast Asian payment-corridor adoption.

XSGD is the rare non-USD stablecoin that exists for a reason beyond novelty — SGD-denominated on-chain liquidity for Southeast Asian payment flows where routing through dollar pairs adds pointless FX friction. The A- is earned: MAS Major Payment Institution license, 100% reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered under regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and twice-monthly independent {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. Past oracle-driven wobbles — the inherent challenge of pricing a SGD token against USD-denominated feeds on thin non-USD pairs — have mostly aged out, leaving a clean peg record with only the occasional brief blip rather than a cluster of alarming-looking spikes. Top-tier liquidity scoring reflects genuine DEX depth spread across many pools rather than one fragile venue, and StraitsX's push into actual payment corridors keeps XSGD anchored to a use case most stablecoins only write blog posts about.

xusd-straitsx.title: Good Bones, No Tenants
xusd-straitsx.text:
Same MAS framework as XSGD, but a single dominant DEX pool against tens of millions in supply makes XUSD institutional plumbing without an on-chain audience.

StraitsX's XUSD inherits the same MAS framework, DBS/StanChart/UOB {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and institutional-grade infrastructure as its XSGD sibling, with regular reserve {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} reports, yet the overall C+ tells the real story: a near-flawless peg and dependency profile dragged down by a D-grade liquidity book. One pool holds essentially everything, and the more than a hundred brief, mostly shallow depeg blips on record are exactly what thin markets produce. The circulating supply is respectable for a Singapore-issued dollar stablecoin, but it lives almost entirely off-chain — the on-chain footprint across its deployments is a ghost town. XUSD's stress signals rarely stray from the calm end of the scale and its redemption backstop earns a solid resilience grade, confirming the institutional plumbing works fine; the problem is that nobody building in DeFi has a reason to choose it over USDC. The value proposition is regional FX corridors and StraitsX's banking relationships, not DEX composability — a perfectly valid business, just not one that shows up in on-chain metrics.

vgbp-vnx.title: The Loneliest Pound
vgbp-vnx.text: VNX's VGBP is Liechtenstein-licensed on-chain British sterling, backed 1:1 by GBP deposits in Swiss and Liechtenstein bank accounts and redeemable through verified issuer accounts. The niche is almost empty: VGBP gives Base, Celo, and Solana users a pound unit, but its market depth is so small that the product still reads more like settlement infrastructure than a liquid trading asset. AREVA's ad-hoc audit and FMA TVTG licensing give the reserve story more formal {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} structure than the on-chain footprint suggests, while same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is the real exit path. The stress gauge is the one dial that actually moves here — pools this thin can push the reading from calm to watchful on modest flows without implying anything about the reserves, and price coverage is sparse enough that Pharos cannot always hold a continuous peg read at all. The UK regulatory wildcard remains existential: if banks or UK-regulated issuers bring serious sterling liquidity on-chain, VGBP's first-mover advantage could vanish.

cusd-cap.title: The Stablecoin Basket Case
cusd-cap.text: cUSD is Cap's diversified basket of regulated stablecoins and tokenized T-bill funds; clever distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one fails. Cap's cUSD is a basket wrapper backed by 35% USDC, 25% USDT, 20% BlackRock's BUIDL, 10% WisdomTree's WTGXX, and 10% PayPal's PYUSD — five institutional-grade stablecoins blended into a single token with a maximum 40% concentration cap per asset. The dynamic-fee vault mechanism adjusts minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} costs in real-time to prevent full utilization, ensuring atomic redemptions remain available, while EigenLayer AVS provides the economic security layer. Redemptions return a proportional basket of all underlying assets rather than a single stablecoin, which socializes any individual reserve depeg across all redeemers — clever risk distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one component fails. Deployed on Ethereum and MegaETH with wrapper-classified governance, cUSD is less an independent stablecoin and more a diversification instrument for holders who want institutional {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure without choosing sides. Cap itself decentralized a notch in late June, launching its CAP governance token after a heavily oversubscribed auction. The BUIDL and WTGXX slices are tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}.

msusd-main-street.title: Redemption Target, Not A Clean Vault
msusd-main-street.text: msUSD is Main Street's dollar token with a USDC redemption target, but Pharos no longer treats it as a clean USDC reserve passthrough. Main Street documents 1:1 USDC minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for verified users, yet the redemption path is capacity-managed, cooldown-bound, and can require position unwinds, asset conversion, and strategy liquidity before settlement. The separate msY token still owns the explicit options-box {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} wrapper, but that split does not independently verify that unstaked msUSD is segregated from liquidity needed to support the strategy. The June 2026 depeg made that distinction material, so Pharos models msUSD with unresolved reserve-verification risk and very-high-risk reserve exposure rather than as fully backed idle USDC.

iusd-infinifi.title: Credit Fund in Token Clothing
iusd-infinifi.text: USDC-collateralized dollar with duration-matched private credit deployment: roughly a fifth of reserves liquid, the rest in 30-day-unwind credit strategies, with redemptions queued under stress. InfiniFi's iUSD routes USDC into institutional private credit — Fasanara, FalconX, Sentora, Maple — behind a liquid DeFi buffer on Spark, Fluid, and Aave, with the siUSD savings wrapper passing through the yield. The structural tension the model was always going to face has now shown up in the grades: a D overall safety grade, dragged down by failing liquidity and resilience marks, because only about a fifth of the backing can be pulled instantly while four-fifths sits locked in credit positions. The peg itself holds cleanly and iUSD rarely strays from the calm end of the stress scale, but a flat stress reading is cold comfort when the real risk is a liquidity wall, not a price wobble. No depeg events recorded yet, which either means the queue is doing exactly its job or that the redemption test that matters has not arrived. Functionally siUSD is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper over private-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} positions, with the buffer-driven {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} queue acting as the gate when liquid reserves run thin — you are earning credit fund returns and bearing credit fund risks through a stablecoin interface.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text: PHT is APACX's Philippine-peso stablecoin built like a Maker-style CDP system, but the beta reserve reality is narrower than the architecture brochure. Current Pharos metadata points to apcxUSDT wrapper collateral as the live reserve line, with apcxUSDC described as planned rather than a proven second leg. That leaves holders with USDT dependency, custodial-wrapper risk, and unresolved privileged mint or admin risk sitting behind a familiar overcollateralized label. The Chainlink PHP/USD oracle and Dutch-auction liquidation design make the mechanism legible, yet the proof path is still thin for a product asking users to trust a new local-currency peg. It is a useful experiment in peso-denominated DeFi rails, but the dashboard reads it as early machinery, not mature monetary infrastructure.

hyusd-hylo.title: Staked SOL, Stable Dollar
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's HYUSD is a Solana dollar whose deployed V1 design lets xSOL absorb volatility for a shared liquid-staking-token pool, a dual-token {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} that asks the loss-absorber to do the unpleasant work before HYUSD holders do. The documented V2 design adds isolated SOL-LST, cbBTC, and USDC pools, but Hylo has not published enough deployment information to reconcile those plans with the current production state. That disclosure gap matters more than a neat mechanism diagram: {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} only comforts holders when they can see which collateral and rules actually govern the token. HYUSD's direct holder controls look comparatively restrained, while its collateral and upgrade surfaces still deserve the kind of attention crypto-backed dollars routinely evade. It is an elegant design with an unfinished audit trail, which is a very DeFi way to make a simple dollar complicated.

meusd-mezo.title: Bitcoin Maxis Get CDPs
meusd-mezo.text: Liquity-style BTC-backed CDP stablecoin on Mezo's Bitcoin L2, with sound redemption mechanics now dragged into D-grade territory by thin liquidity and concentrated control; persistent above-peg drift from defensive overcollateralization. Mezo's meUSD applies Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics to Bitcoin collateral — 110% minimum ratio, permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 75 bps, atomic settlement — across native and wrapped BTC variants on a Bitcoin L2 that Pharos classifies as unproven. The headline D grade tells a split story: peg health is genuinely strong at A-, but it sits next to a D liquidity score and an F on decentralization, and those two drag the overall down to where the design no longer rescues it. The peg drifts above par in the way BTC-backed CDPs tend to — borrowers overcollateralize defensively when Bitcoin volatility spikes — and meUSD has logged hundreds of brief deviation events with a worst-case push to roughly +591 bps. The decentralization mark is earned: the Ethereum surface runs through a 5/9 Safe and a Wormhole NTT manager that can raise its own mint cap, so "permissionless borrowing on Mezo" coexists with very real admin keys off-chain. DEWS has lately drifted toward the watchful end of the stress scale rather than sitting calm, which fits a thin two-chain deployment where DEX liquidity remains shallow for any serious exit scenario.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: Undercollateralized by Design
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance was refreshingly honest about what it was: an intentionally undercollateralized stablecoin at roughly 40% backing, minted through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve, TermMax, and Morpho vault positions, designed explicitly for professional market participants who could price the risk. Apparently they priced it — supply has since been all but wound down in a sharp, near-total contraction, and the issuer's transparency endpoint now reports backing roughly equal to the little that remains outstanding. The C+ safety grade is less a vote of confidence than arithmetic: a nearly empty book is easy to cover one-for-one, and thin, single-venue exit liquidity matters less when there is almost nothing left to exit. The modular adapter architecture — dynamic Curve liquidity management, fixed-rate TermMax lending, Morpho vault integration — was genuinely interesting engineering, but building sophisticated infrastructure around a product that deliberately skipped the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} step is the kind of experiment that works until it doesn't. USDU's distinction is ending in the rare exit lane: wound down in orderly fashion before the market could write the depeg headline.

uty-xsy.title: Frozen on the Avalanche
uty-xsy.text: XSY's UTY is an AVAX-hedged {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar custodied at Ceffu and Copper with a 7-day unbonding, and it reads less like an operating product than a locked vault on a quiet mountain. Supply has the look of something in stasis rather than active use, and the F safety grade reflects that: an F on liquidity and an F on resilience drag the composite down regardless of how tidily the peg itself behaves. The {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} AVAX {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} (35% long spot, 35% short perps, 30% USDC) is custodied at Ceffu and Copper {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with Accountable attestations, but the 7-day unbonding period and thin, fallback-class DEX coverage make exit an exercise in patience. On the actual peg, UTY barely registers stress — it sits at the calm end of the stress scale, and its dozens of recorded deviations are brief blips that never crested 300 basis points, which is unusually contained for an F-rated coin. The peg mechanism evidently works when anyone bothers to test it; the problem is that almost nobody does.

gusd-gate.title: Exchange Scrip, Treasury Wrapper
gusd-gate.text: Gate USD is Gate's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} dollar minted 1:1 from USDT/USDC deposits, backed by 70% {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 25% stablecoins with 5% opaque CEX-managed strategies. Gate USD functions less as a stablecoin and more as a yield certificate: users deposit USDT or USDC on Gate, receive GUSD, and reclaim principal plus interest at {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The reserve is 70% short-term Treasuries and 25% stablecoin deposits, but that final 5% in undisclosed CEX-managed yield strategies is the opacity that drags the safety grade to C. At $158M circulating from the Cayman Islands with exactly one DEX pool (HHI of 1.0 — maximum possible concentration), the on-chain exit route is effectively decorative. Nine depeg events with a tight 171 bps worst deviation suggest the peg mechanism works, but only because almost nobody tries to exit through DeFi. The 65-rated offchain redemption via Gate's own platform means your exit depends entirely on the exchange remaining operational and willing.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: TradFi's On-Chain Experiment
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SocGen-FORGE's USDCV is MiCA-regulated bank-issued plumbing with cash at BNY Mellon, institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and stress readings that have usually looked almost comically calm. It is what happens when one of Europe's largest banks decides to issue a stablecoin: 100% USD cash in bankruptcy-remote segregated accounts, an ACPR-regulated EMI license, and daily self-reported reserve disclosure. The live grade now sits a notch below the old headline because reach matters: two-chain deployment, concentrated DEX liquidity, and multi-day settlement through SG-FORGE's issuer portal limit the on-chain usefulness. The peg record is still one of the cleaner ones in the dashboard, which is exactly what the reserve design was built to deliver. The tension is not solvency; it is distribution. TradFi brought excellent paperwork on-chain, then discovered the market does not automatically provide liquidity as a courtesy.

usdai-usd-ai.title: The Liquid Base Token
usdai-usd-ai.text: USDai is the non-yielding base token in USD.AI, and the important current detail is that Pharos metadata shows the base reserve as 100% PYUSD held by the USDai contract. USDC and USDT are deposit and exit currencies for users, not the assets currently sitting underneath the base token, which is exactly the kind of distinction stablecoin marketing tends to blur when nobody is watching. The GPU-backed loan book belongs to sUSDai, the separate staking sleeve, so base USDai holders are taking PYUSD dependency and platform-admin risk rather than AI-credit yield risk. The real-time proof-of-reserves API is a genuine transparency upgrade, especially for a young product spread across multiple chains. The catch is centralized mint and upgrade control through bridge/admin roles and a Safe-governed path, so the base token is liquid and observable, not permissionless.

susdai-usd-ai.title: The GPU-Credit Sleeve
susdai-usd-ai.text: sUSDai is where USD.AI moves from a PYUSD-backed base dollar into the actual AI-credit bet. The reserve stack currently combines a large PYUSD liquid sleeve with a smaller but meaningful GPU-backed infrastructure-loan sleeve, so the token behaves like a NAV-appreciating credit product rather than a clean payment stablecoin. Accountable-style real-time reserve visibility helps separate the liquid assets from the loan book, which is useful because GPU collateral is not cash no matter how fashionable the acronym is. Exits run through staking mechanics and a queued withdrawal flow, not a simple always-on issuer redemption promise. The exit story improved at the margin in June, when USD.AI stood up a $100 million liquidity facility with Fluid — a real secondary venue, though a facility is a buffer, not a bottomless bid. sUSDai may be the interesting product in the USD.AI pair, but it is also where the yield stops being free and starts being underwriting.

usx-solstice.title: The Solana Wrapper
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is a Solana wrapper minted 1:1 against 55% USDC and 45% USDT, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve and KYC-gated institutional minting — inheriting its underlying stablecoins' safety rather than creating its own. Solstice's USX is structurally simpler than its Swiss pedigree and Galaxy Digital backing might suggest: 55% USDC and 45% USDT, minted 1:1, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve verifying the reserves on-chain. Classified as a wrapper with governance quality reflecting its pass-through nature, USX inherits the safety profile of its underlying stablecoins rather than creating its own — which makes the value proposition a question of Solana-native convenience rather than novel design. The KYC-gated institutional minting at a $500K minimum coexists with permissionless DEX access, creating a two-tier system where large minters get direct access and everyone else trades the secondary market. Plans to expand collateral to SOL, ETH, and BTC would change the risk profile entirely, but for now USX is a regulated stablecoin wrapper on a chain that already has USDC and USDT.

hollar-hydrated.title: Aave Fork, Polkadot Address
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is an Aave V3 fork on Hydration with diversified DOT, ETH, BTC, and stablecoin collateral plus HSM-anchored peg swaps. The core mechanics are a multi-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with per-block partial {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, and a Stability Module that behaves like a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}. That design earns structural credit, but everything runs on a chain Pharos still treats as unproven, which caps the ceiling no matter how tidy the fork looks. The live profile has slipped slightly, mostly because concentrated DEX liquidity and small-market demand leave the peg with little shock absorption. HOLLAR's viability ultimately tracks whether Polkadot DeFi expands or contracts — a bet that has not paid off for most Polkadot-native projects to date. The product is more coherent than the ecosystem around it, which is not the comfort its holders probably wanted.

musd-metamask.title: Distribution as Moat
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask mUSD is what happens when a wallet with tens of millions of users decides to vertically integrate — issued by Stripe's Bridge on M0 protocol rails, with 85% in {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 15% in bankruptcy-remote cash verified by real-time on-chain {{term:attestation}}validator attestations{{/term}}. The B- safety grade reflects a split decision: near-flawless peg behavior and institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that rarely leaves the calm end of the stress scale, dragged down by a wholly centralized control model and liquidity that earns no better than a passing grade. The reserve composition reads like a compliance team's wishlist, but the secondary market hasn't fully caught up with primary-market confidence — a few dozen brief depeg blips, including a 557-bps positive spike, show that arbitrage works in theory while DEX liquidity stays spread wide and shallow. The funnel switched on at the end of June: MetaMask's new Money Account wires mUSD into yield routes and card spending directly inside the wallet, the first serious attempt to convert those tens of millions of users into float. The moat narrative is still more aspiration than balance sheet — but the plumbing to realize it now exists.

cash-phantom.title: The Wallet's Dollar
cash-phantom.text: CASH is Phantom's wallet-native dollar on Solana, T-bill backed by Bridge Building Inc.; distribution edge over decentralization. Phantom's CASH leverages what no DeFi protocol can replicate: distribution through crypto's most popular Solana wallet, giving millions of users a native stablecoin without requiring them to understand anything about stablecoin infrastructure. Under the hood, Bridge Building Inc. backs CASH with {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, reverse repos, {{term:money-market-fund}}government money-market funds{{/term}}, bank deposits, and a 10% allocation to tokenized treasuries including BUIDL — 90% of reserves in very-low-risk assets with bankruptcy-remote segregation under FinCEN and state money transmitter licenses. The B- report card reflects a genuinely stable product: a handful of depeg events, none worse than 181 bps, and a peg that rarely strays from the calm end of the stress scale, while over $72M in DEX liquidity across Solana pools provides workable exit depth. Solana-only deployment is a feature, not a limitation — CASH exists to be Phantom's default dollar, and the growing supply suggests that for wallet-native users, the trade-off between decentralization purity and tap-to-buy convenience was decided before it was ever offered. That default status now extends to new surfaces: World, the fully on-chain prediction market unveiled inside Phantom, settles winning positions in CASH — the clearest sign yet that Phantom intends CASH to be the unit of account for everything the wallet touches. Bankruptcy-remote {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backs 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}; the BUIDL slice is a tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure.

tgbp-tokenised.title: The FCA's First Bet
tgbp-tokenised.text: tGBP is a pound stablecoin with the sensible reserve mix you would expect from a UK-facing issuer: GBP cash, money-market exposure, and short-term government paper. BCP Technologies' FCA cryptoasset registration and monthly independent attestation give the product more institutional shape than the average local-currency stablecoin. The tradeoff is not reserve exoticism but issuer centralization, since mint, burn, and upgrade control still sit behind a highly concentrated owner path. Redemption is a direct off-chain GBP workflow, which is appropriate for sterling rails and less composable than DeFi users usually pretend they want. In a market full of dollar clones, tGBP is refreshingly specific; the question is whether UK demand is large enough to make that specificity matter.

eurau-allunity.title: Deutsche Boerse's Euro Bet
eurau-allunity.text: EURAU is AllUnity's MiCA-licensed EUR stablecoin; full-reserve bank deposits, broad L2 reach, top-tier institutional sponsorship. AllUnity's EURAU is backed 100% by euro deposits at CRR-eligible EU credit institutions, BaFin-licensed as an EMI under MiCA, with institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and integration into Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream infrastructure — more institutional credibility than most euro stablecoins combined. Backed by DWS (Deutsche Bank's asset management arm), Galaxy Digital, and Flow Traders, the sponsor list reads like a TradFi-crypto {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} roster. Deployed across five EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon), EURAU has broader L2 reach than competing euro stablecoins that remain Ethereum-only. The problem is the denominator: euro stablecoins represent a fraction of the global stablecoin market, making EURAU simultaneously one of the best-backed euro tokens and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar dominates this space. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through AllUnity.

usdh-native-markets.title: The Evacuated Beachhead
usdh-native-markets.text: Native Markets' USDH on HyperEVM is a Bridge-issued (Stripe) dollar with 40% short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at JP Morgan plus tokenized treasuries — a bet on Hyperliquid traction that ended in a structured wind-down. USDH built to nine figures on HyperEVM with one of the more credible reserve compositions in the market: 40% short-term T-bills managed by BlackRock at JP Morgan, 20% tokenized {{term:treasury}}treasuries{{/term}} via BUIDL and USTB, and the rest in cash, repos, and {{term:money-market-fund}}treasury funds{{/term}} — all flowing through Bridge Building Inc., Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary. The 12 depeg events with swings as wide as 227 basis points tell the story of a young stablecoin on a single chain still building the arbitrage infrastructure to enforce its peg tightly. The bet did not get to play out: in late May Native Markets announced a structured wind-down as Coinbase took over as Hyperliquid's official USDC treasury deployer, the deployer liquidated its unlocked HYPE allocation, and by mid-June USDH's markets were settled and delisted. The validator vote that chose USDH over Paxos and Ethena was a bet on revenue redirection from Circle; the ecosystem re-voted with its treasury, and the beachhead is being evacuated in orderly fashion.

sbc-brale.title: Infrastructure Demo Reel
sbc-brale.text:
Brale's SBC tripled to $12.2M with very-low-risk reserves and broader chain distribution than tokens 50x its size — a reference implementation for its stablecoin-as-a-service platform.

Brale's SBC tripled from $3.9M to $12.2M in the past month — the fastest proportional growth in the tracked set — yet its safety grade has slipped to B-, dragged down by a liquidity grade that lands near the bottom of the scale. The backing is not the problem: reserves are 100% very-low-risk, split evenly between cash and short-duration {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, deployed across 10 chains from a FinCEN-licensed money transmitter with regulated bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and zero-fee {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The tension the grade reflects is the one this token was always going to live with: a recurring series of brief depeg blips and an effective DEX TVL of just $5M spread thin across a 10-chain footprint, broader distribution than tokens fifty times its size can claim. That is entirely the point — this is a reference implementation for Brale's stablecoin-as-a-service platform, not a consumer product. SBC exists so Brale can tell enterprise clients their infrastructure works — and the conversations now include Visa, which ran a June proof-of-concept exploring SBC-based institutional settlement on Canton — while the tripling supply suggests the pitch is landing; the slipping grade just confirms that distribution breadth is not the same as liquidity depth.

euri-banking-circle.title: The Binance Distribution Play
euri-banking-circle.text: EURI is Banking Circle's MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin with fee-free 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} — a {{term:custody}}credit-institution{{/term}} wrapper engineered for Binance distribution. Eurite exists because Binance needed a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin and Banking Circle had the Luxembourg CSSF credit institution license to provide one — 70% euro cash in segregated fiduciary accounts, 30% EU government securities, Ernst & Young {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, all the regulatory furniture arranged correctly. The peg side of that wrapper is impeccable: an A+ peg, a DEWS reading parked at the calm end of the stress scale, and not a single depeg on record. What drags the overall grade down to C+ is liquidity, which sits at an outright F — Binance's endorsement clearly does not translate into organic on-chain trading depth. With no yield product and deployment limited to Ethereum and BSC, Eurite is less a standalone stablecoin and more a compliance wrapper that lets Binance's European users stay in euros without leaving the exchange's orbit.

msusd-metronome.title: Synths Still Standing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD is a synthetic dollar from the pre-yield-farming era that somehow kept its users, minted against USDC, DAI, ETH, WBTC, sfrxETH, and Vesper yield tokens through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}. There is no direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for the token; users repay debt to recover collateral, while zero-slippage internal synth swaps and collateral-provider buybacks are meant to close discounts. That makes the peg mechanism clever but distinctly circular: price support depends on the people already inside the system finding the balance-sheet trade worth taking. The collateral basket also imports risks from major stablecoins and legacy DeFi yield wrappers. msUSD is not trying to be the market's reserve asset; it is a durable niche synth, which is both its achievement and its ceiling.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit in a Token
aznd-mu-digital.text: AZND is Mu Digital's KYC-gated, NAV-bearing dollar token backed by a Singapore-regulated Asia credit fund, with a muBOND junior tranche absorbing first losses — structured credit dressed as a stablecoin. Mu Digital's AZND wraps an Asian credit fund into a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin on Monad, managed by Singapore-regulated Golden Hill Asset Management with a muBOND junior tranche providing {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} — it is a structured credit product wearing a stablecoin's clothing. Accountable's real-time dashboard currently shows reserves concentrated in short-term cash (81%) and liquid bonds (19%), a notably more conservative posture than the published mandate targeting up to 20% illiquid private credit. The report card sits at a C, and the discount is earned: the single-chain Monad deployment, concentrated DEX liquidity (HHI of 0.72 across just 2 pools), and weekly KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} settling over days mean exit options are genuinely constrained, which drags liquidity into D-grade territory. Supply has contracted roughly 20% in the past week alone, suggesting early holders are testing those redemption mechanics in practice. AZND targets a real gap — institutional Asian credit exposure on-chain — but the question is whether DeFi-native capital will accept fund-style lockups for single-digit yields.

nect-beraborrow.title: Liquity on Life Support
nect-beraborrow.text: Liquity v2-style CDP stablecoin on Berachain backed by an exotic collateral zoo (iBGT, WBERA, BTC/ETH derivatives, LP tokens); sub-million supply and razor-thin liquidity stop the redemption mechanism from doing its job. BeraBorrow's NECT runs Liquity-v2 {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics on Berachain's exotic collateral zoo — 40% iBGT, 25% WBERA, plus wrapped BTC variants, ETH derivatives, and Kodiak LP tokens, all classified high-risk on an unproven chain. The D overall grade is earned, not harsh: NECT has logged hundreds of brief sub-peg blips with a worst deviation past 750 bps, it is sitting in an active depeg right now, and it spends most of its time on the cautionary half of the stress scale rather than the calm end. With a sub-million circulating supply and thin DEX liquidity, the coin is barely above the threshold where the CDP {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism can function as designed — you need arbitrageurs to show up, and the economics don't justify it at this scale. The collateral-redemption backstop and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffer remain structurally sound on paper, but sound mechanisms need liquid markets to express themselves.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token with 50% in a Turkish lira {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} via Balsa Technologies, 40% in DeFi protocols, and 10% in stablecoin buffer — KYC-gated with whitelisted queue redemption. PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token — 50% deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy via Balsa Technologies ({{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} TRY/USD trades capturing Turkey's inflation-driven {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} carry), 40% across DeFi protocols (Giza, Almanak, USD.AI, Ethena, Aave, Cap), and 10% in a USDC/USDT buffer. The very-high risk classification on the Turkish FX strategy and high risk on the DeFi allocations are reflected in the exotic collateral quality rating and a backstop of 65 with whitelisted queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 0.2% fee — KYC/KYB required to mint or redeem, with a 24-hour FIFO settlement queue. It's a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi — Turkish carry trade returns are uncorrelated with crypto markets — but also one that concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market whose currency has lost over 90% against the dollar in a decade. The NAV has appreciated above $1.07, which proves the strategy works when it works — but half the float has queued out inside a month, so a meaningful share of holders decided not to wait around for the answer to what happens when it doesn't.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold Bars, Sky Strings
pmusd-precious-metals.text: Gold-backed supply paired with a sUSDS-funded {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} means pmUSD's peg defense depends on Sky Protocol staying healthy — a meaningful external dependency. The structure runs on two awkward logics: supply is backed by gold via RAAC's RWf(x) fork and ION.au tokenized claims, while dollar recovery relies on a PSM holding Sky's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} savings wrapper. Arbitrageurs can swap discounted pmUSD for sUSDS at a $1 internal valuation, but the flow is one-directional and halts if sUSDS reserves fall below the module's threshold. That ties pmUSD's dollar recovery to Sky stability, which is a strange dependency for a coin whose collateral narrative begins with precious metals. That failure mode is no longer hypothetical: pmUSD is currently trading far below the dollar — a four-figure-basis-point gap with the stress gauge at alert — and the report card has collapsed to an F while the one-directional PSM does what it can from its side of the door. Real-time Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} document the gold backing with genuine rigor; the question is whether gold is the right asset to stabilize with someone else's savings-dollar plumbing.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Three Layers to Treasuries
jupusd-jupiter.text: Solana dollar from Jupiter, 90% backed by Ethena USDtb (BlackRock BUIDL) + 10% USDC; pristine collateral buried under three wrappers. JupUSD is Jupiter's play to own Solana's dollar layer: 90% backed by Ethena's USDtb (itself a wrapper around BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized Treasury fund) with a 10% USDC buffer, custodied by Porto via Anchorage Digital. The dependency chain runs JupUSD to USDtb to BUIDL to actual government bonds — pristine collateral buried under three layers of operational and counterparty risk. At $80M circulating and growing 11% month-over-month, adoption is real, with $12M in DEX TVL though heavily concentrated (HHI of 0.71) in a few pools. A handful of shallow depeg events, none deeper than about -202 bps, and a stress reading that rarely leaves the calm end of the scale suggest a clean launch, while the backstop offers atomic settlement through whitelisted on-chain redemption into stablecoins. The C grade prices in the dependency complexity and centralized governance — Jupiter is betting that BlackRock's brand travels well enough through intermediaries that Solana users won't mind the wrapper tax. The reserve trace lands in BUIDL's {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} via Anchorage {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with whitelisted atomic {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} into USDC as the peg floor.

u-united-stables.title: Variable Reserve Wrapper
u-united-stables.text: United Stables U is a centralized dollar token whose reserve policy is deliberately flexible: cash, U.S. Treasury bills, and approved fiat-referenced stablecoins can all sit in the basket. That flexibility is operationally convenient and analytically annoying, because the composition can move without the clean fixed-slice story users prefer. Pharos records a real-time issuer dashboard, which is better than a PDF fossil, but it is still self-attested transparency rather than independent audit discipline. The smart-contract framing promises minting only after collateral receipt and burns on redemption, while token ownership resolves to a small Safe controlling admin authority. U is trying to be a programmable reserve wrapper; the risk is that the wrapper's discretion is the product.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Insurance Capital Goes On-Chain
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD is a NAV-appreciating token that channels deposits into ETH basis trades, short-duration T-bills, and a USDC instant-redemption buffer. The reserve split reads like reinsurance float deployed across DeFi yield sources: half the book rides on USDe and sUSDe {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}}, with Treasuries and USDC cushioning the exit path. The live grade has improved from the older summary's read, but the upgrade does not erase the central dependency: Ethena infrastructure is doing a lot of work inside the collateral stack. Multi-chain deployment and real secondary-market depth make reUSD more usable than many yield tokens wearing a dollar label. Queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, 20% immediate capacity, and BVI licensing will not satisfy conservative compliance teams, but the Chainlink/Network Firm real-time {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} layer helps. It remains one of the more intellectually honest yield products on the market, which is not the same as being simple.

rwausdi-multipli.title: The RWA Middleware Layer
rwausdi-multipli.text:
A KYB-gated UAE wrapper aggregating 100+ tokenized T-bills, gold, and market-neutral funds — with a Lloyd's de-pegging insurance policy that's a genuinely novel backstop.

Multipli's rwaUSDi wraps 100+ tokenized treasury products, gold tokens, and market-neutral fund units into a single mintable stablecoin — 50% in tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} (BUIDL, USDY, OUSG), 25% in aggregated treasury-backed stablecoins, 15% in tokenized gold, and 10% in institutional fund units from Nomura, Fasanara, and Edge Capital. The pitch is that lending protocols can't individually underwrite hundreds of {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} tokens, so rwaUSDi does the aggregation and due diligence — backed by a Lloyd's insurance policy covering de-pegging risk, which is a genuinely novel backstop for a stablecoin. UAE-domiciled with AFI-audited on-chain reserves, it has spread from Ethereum across Base, Arbitrum, and Monad while keeping KYB-gated institutional minting, making it less a retail product and more a composable RWA building block. The elegant abstraction adds a trust layer between holder and underlying assets, but with 99 peg score and only two depeg events on record, the machinery has functioned as designed.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} yield from Ethena's USDtb (90% of backing, itself holding BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}) to subsidize network operations — the chain literally gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. The peg itself holds flawlessly and the asset has logged only a couple of brief deviations, but it has lately drifted off the calm end of the stress scale into watch territory, and the absence of any tracked DEX liquidity means exit routes are limited to the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism. The dependency on Ethena's infrastructure for both reserve management and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} adds counterparty risk that the underlying Treasuries don't carry, and it shows in the grading: a middling C overall, weighed down by thin liquidity and a dependency profile that inherits USDtb's concentrated mint authority wholesale. The stablecoin's value proposition is inseparable from MegaETH's own traction as an L2 — a flywheel where stablecoin adoption subsidizes network costs which drives adoption, elegant when it works, but the flywheel spins in both directions.

usdm-monetrix.title: HyperEVM's USDC Wrapper
usdm-monetrix.text: Monetrix USDM is the base dollar token in a small HyperEVM yield stack: USDC backs liquid USDM, while sUSDM is the separate staking wrapper where the strategy exposure lives. That split matters because Pharos can admit USDM through DefiLlama supply plus CoinGecko pricing, but sUSDM still lacks a maintained market-cap and price source in the runtime pipeline. The reserve story is therefore straightforward but narrow: USDM inherits USDC issuer risk and Monetrix smart-contract/operations risk, while the dashboard transparency is self-reported rather than an independent attestation. It is useful coverage for HyperEVM dollar liquidity, not yet a fully modeled yield product.

usat-tether.title: Tether Goes Domestic
usat-tether.text: Tether's USA-T is a GENIUS-era U.S. dollar issued 1:1 by Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC federal charter, backed roughly 80% by {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-collateralized reverse repos and 20% cash, with Cantor Fitzgerald {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and monthly Deloitte {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} disclosures — the cleanest regulatory setup Tether has ever assembled. The B- report card reflects a product that holds its peg cleanly and rarely strays from the calm end of the stress scale, with no depeg events on record, but hasn't had time to build a track record either way. The real drag is liquidity, which sits at a D grade: the Ethereum-only deployment and thin DEX presence mean USA-T is still distribution-light, and the peg's pristine reads owe as much to youth as to depth. The strategic logic is transparent: USA-T is Tether's answer to USDC on US soil, separating the domestic compliance story from USDT's offshore empire, with a 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise through Anchorage. Whether American institutions will trust a Tether-branded dollar after a decade of skepticism is the open question — and until liquidity catches up to the compliance story, the answer stays unproven.

yzusd-yuzu.title: Yield Vault in Stable Clothing
yzusd-yuzu.text:
A KYC-gated yield aggregator on Plasma minted 1:1 with USDT0, with a junior tranche absorbing first losses and zero secondary market to test the peg.

Yuzu's yzUSD packages curated DeFi yield strategies into an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin — 50% Pendle PT/LP positions, 20% Euler/Morpho lending, 20% other DeFi strategies, and a 10% USDT0 buffer — all classified as exotic collateral on an unproven chain (Plasma). A perfect peg score and zero depeg events sound reassuring until you note the absence of any DEX liquidity and queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} scoring just 56 on the backstop, with the yzPP junior tranche absorbing first losses. The strict KYC gating — only accredited, qualified, or institutional investors can mint and redeem — makes yzUSD one of the most access-restricted stablecoins in DeFi, which explains both the zero depeg events (few holders means few sellers) and the non-existent secondary market. It's a yield aggregator that happens to maintain a dollar peg rather than a stablecoin that happens to generate yield — the distinction matters when things go wrong.

nusd-neutrl.title: The Contraction Test
nusd-neutrl.text: Delta-neutral synthetic dollar backed mainly by stablecoins plus hedged OTC positions; weathering a deep, months-long supply contraction without breaking peg, with whitelisted queue-based redemption and a yield-bearing sNUSD wrapper. Neutrl's NUSD has been stress-tested by something more revealing than a depeg event: a contraction that erased a quarter of supply in a single month and has kept grinding lower since, as holders queue for the exit. The {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar backed by 93.5% stablecoins with OTC and hedged {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions in a {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} structure has held its peg cleanly through the drawdown — only a handful of shallow sub-200-bps blips on record — which says more about the mechanism than any bull-market AUM figure could. The composite grade, which slipped while the outflow was at its worst, has recovered to a B- as the mechanism kept clearing redemptions without drama — the dashboard's quiet acknowledgment that surviving an exit queue is itself a credential. The peg engine is still doing its job with the quiet competence of a product built for exactly this scenario; whether the shrunken base settles into a core of committed holders or keeps draining is the question the next quarter answers — and the scoring, at least, has stopped leaning toward the pessimistic reading.

usdgo-osl.title: The Quiet Surge
usdgo-osl.text: OSL's USDGO has been compounding supply at triple-digit monthly rates with a near-perfect peg, backed by T-bills and cash at Anchorage Digital under an OCC charter — on-chain liquidity is the bottleneck, not credentials. USDGO has kept compounding at a rate that makes most stablecoin launches look lethargic — supply has multiplied again since spring and now sits in the high hundreds of millions — all while holding a near-perfect peg. The safety grade has settled back to a C+ as on-chain liquidity strains to keep pace with issuance, but the reserve stack keeps upgrading: Treasury bills and cash under an OCC federal bank charter, now diversified across tokenized money-market funds from JPMorgan, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs — credentials that outclass most competitors several times its size, with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Thin on-chain depth against a nine-figure float makes this an issuer-API exit story rather than an on-chain arbitrage play, with OSL's institutional pipeline doing the heavy lifting. The old question was whether the surge was one-time onboarding; several consecutive months of steep growth suggest the Asia-Pacific institutional pipeline is a durable bid — the question now is whether the on-chain plumbing ever catches up to it.

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Trillion-Dollar Entrance
