The current live checks validate on-chain supply, while higher-grade bullion reconciliation depends on Matrixdock reserve data granular enough to match issuer {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} metrics against token supply. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} is available through Matrixdock for KYC-approved users, but public fee and capacity terms remain issuer-process dependent.

gramg-token-teknoloji.title: Turkey's Gram-Gold Token
gramg-token-teknoloji.text: GRAMG is Token Teknoloji's Turkish gram-gold stablecoin backed by physical gold at Turkish bank custodians, with issuer-published proof but no machine-readable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. Token Teknoloji's GRAMG is a one-gram gold stablecoin with reserve materials pointing to Turkish bank custody. The Avalanche deployment has meaningful live supply, so Pharos tracks that chain first and uses CoinGecko commodity coverage for market data. The reserve proof is weaker than a machine-readable attestation, but stronger than a pure marketing claim because the issuer publishes bank-backed proof materials. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop remains unscored because public direct-holder redemption terms are not specific enough.

grams-token-teknoloji.title: Turkey's Gram-Silver Token
grams-token-teknoloji.text: GRAMS is Token Teknoloji's Turkish gram-silver stablecoin backed by physical silver at Turkish bank {{term:custody}}custodians{{/term}}, with supply liveness over independent reserve reconciliation. GRAMS mirrors Token Teknoloji's gold product for silver, with one token representing one gram of physical silver. The research packet found enough issuer reserve material and live Avalanche supply to add the asset, but no clean public reserve API. Pharos therefore treats the live feed as supply liveness over curated reserves rather than independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} remains unmodeled until direct holder terms, limits, and capacity are documented.

euroe-membrane.title: Redemption-Only EUROe
euroe-membrane.text: EUROe is now best read in the past tense, which is not where a growth stablecoin wants to live. Membrane's Finnish EMI-licensed euro token has moved into Paxos' redemption-only wind-down after the product line was decommissioned, leaving holders with a 1:1 EUR exit path rather than an expanding on-chain euro network. The old reserve story was straightforward euro fiat and euro-denominated assets, but the current proof source is a redemption notice, not an ongoing reserve machine. Pharos still records the multichain contracts and regulated-entity posture, while the mint authority history shows EOA admin control and no heroic decentralization epilogue. EUROe's lesson is blunt: regulatory seriousness can make wind-down orderly, but it cannot make a discontinued token relevant.

gbpm-mento.title: Mento's CDP Pound
gbpm-mento.text: GBPm is Mento's British pound stablecoin on Celo, minted from {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} collateralized by USDm with oracle-priced {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. GBPm extends Mento's Celo FX stablecoin set into sterling using USDm-collateralized CDP rows rather than the older shared reserve basket alone. Mento's dashboard API exposes GBPm troves, turning live collateral and debt into visible reserve evidence. That makes the entry useful despite a modest supply footprint because the backing path is visible and cheap to maintain. The primary risk is dependency on Mento oracles, Celo execution, and USDm collateral quality.

jpym-mento.title: Mento's CDP Yen
jpym-mento.text: Small CDP yen on Celo backed by USDm collateral via Mento troves; CoinGecko-admitted, Mento API exposes live CDP collateral. JPYm is a small but active yen stablecoin on Celo, backed by USDm collateral in Mento CDP troves. Pharos uses CoinGecko admission because DefiLlama's JPYm supply row is zero, while the Mento API still exposes live CDP collateral. The Mento API keeps reserve visibility aligned with GBPm and CHFm. JPYm is tracked for strategic non-USD coverage, with liquidity and oracle dependency as the main caveats. As a Mento FX stablecoin, JPYm rests on a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with USDm {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and oracle-priced FPMM swaps acting as the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} surface against the reserve.

chfm-mento.title: Mento's CDP Franc
chfm-mento.text: CHFm is a Mento CDP-backed Swiss franc stablecoin on Celo, minted against USDm collateral rather than fiat reserves. CHFm gives Pharos another Swiss-franc stablecoin, but with a very different risk profile from fiat-backed VCHF or Frankencoin. Its reserves are USDm collateral posted into Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} troves, and Mento live data exposes those rows directly. The asset is small, but the backing path is visible enough for reserve tracking. The residual risks are the Celo/Mento mechanism, USDm collateral path, and thin secondary liquidity. {{term:overcollateralization}}Overcollateralization{{/term}} and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} logic inside Mento drive peg maintenance.

bfusd-binance.title: Binance's Account Dollar
bfusd-binance.text: BFUSD is a Binance account product redeemable inside Binance against USD stablecoins, backed by an opaque collateral pool and a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} hedging portfolio — not a normal on-chain stablecoin. BFUSD is included because it has meaningful CoinGecko coverage and a large Binance user footprint, but it is not a normal on-chain stablecoin. The product lives inside Binance accounts, earns Binance-set rewards, and is {{term:redemption}}redeemable{{/term}} only through Binance-controlled terms that allow limits, fees, delays, and suspension. Pharos therefore treats the reserve stack as very-high-risk opaque exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rather than independent proof. The entry is useful for market coverage, not for permissionless DeFi composability.

pathusd-bridge.title: Tempo's Bridge Dollar
pathusd-bridge.text: Bridge-issued dollar quote token for Tempo, backed by institutional reserves and redeemable through Bridge-supported flows; matters more as a payment-chain rail than for current scale. pathUSD is the Bridge-issued dollar quote token for Tempo, backed by a conventional reserve portfolio and redeemable back through Bridge-supported {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flows. The asset matters less because of current scale than because it is native to a payment-focused chain that may become an important stablecoin rail. The risk profile is straightforward: institutional reserve assets and issuer redemption on the strong side, new-chain execution and limited independent reserve telemetry on the weak side.

djed-coti.title: Cardano's Reserve-Coin Stable
djed-coti.text: DJED is Cardano's formally designed reserve-coin stablecoin, not a borrower CDP wearing a different hat. ADA sits in the reserve, DJED is the dollar claim, and SHEN absorbs surplus and volatility inside the protocol's 400% to 800% reserve-ratio band. That design gives the peg a clear mechanical buffer, but it also ties the whole system to ADA collateral risk and to the COTI/IOG oracle role. The minting policy is materially constrained by Cardano smart-contract rules rather than a discretionary issuer desk, which is a real structural virtue. DJED is one of the cleaner algorithmic-adjacent designs, though crypto has earned the right to treat every reserve-coin elegance proof as an invitation to ask what happens when the reserve asset has a bad month.

usdv-solomon.title: The Ceffu Strategy Dollar
usdv-solomon.text: Solomon's USDv is a Solana stablecoin backed by Ceffu-custodied {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} margin, with aggregate disclosure but no live composition feed and no documented holder redemption path. Solomon USDv is a Solana stablecoin backed by Ceffu-custodied strategy assets and off-exchange {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} margin via {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} positions. The public supply is easy to validate on-chain, but the reserve disclosure is aggregate and does not expose a live composition API. That keeps the Pharos entry conservative: useful for tracking a visible Solana dollar, but not a high-confidence reserve model. Without a documented holder {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route and with all collateral sitting in Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the backstop remains intentionally unmodeled.

xai-silo-finance.title: Silo's Credit-Line Dollar
xai-silo-finance.text:
A Silo Finance CDP dollar minted against approved isolated-market collateral; risk is governance, liquidation quality, and venue-thin secondary liquidity.

XAI is a Silo Finance credit-line stablecoin: users borrow it against approved Silo collateral and repay it to close debt, while SiloDAO controls the credit-line parameters. Pharos validates Ethereum supply and carries the reserve stack as curated Silo collateral rather than a full live vault decomposition. The risk is classic {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} risk in a narrow venue: governance parameters, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffers, {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} quality, and whether secondary liquidity can enforce the peg when borrow demand changes.

fxd-fathom.title: XDC's Native CDP Dollar
fxd-fathom.text: FXD is Fathom's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-minted dollar on XDC, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by XDC and stabilized by {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} plus a stability module. Fathom Dollar gives the XDC ecosystem a native overcollateralized dollar backed by XDC and Fathom collateral-pool positions. It is tracked for chain coverage and DefiLlama visibility despite modest scale. The design is familiar CDP plumbing — mint against collateral, burn to repay, liquidate weak positions, and use a stability module for peg support — but the collateral base and chain liquidity make it materially riskier than larger Ethereum CDP systems.

usp-pareto-credit.title: Private Credit With a Dollar Wrapper
usp-pareto-credit.text: Pareto USP is a dollar token whose reserve stack is mostly Pareto private-credit vault exposure, with small USDC and USDS buffers doing the polite work of pretending liquidity is simple. Verified users can mint and redeem through Pareto, while open-market holders still rely on secondary liquidity or the privilege of becoming eligible. That access split is the product's central tension: the backing may earn credit yield, but private credit is not the same exit profile as cash, T-bills, or a permissionless collateral redemption path. Pharos keeps the reserve risk high and surfaces the soft-depeg notice because the market has already shown it can price that mismatch. USP is a credit product with a dollar ticker, and the ticker is the least informative part.

dllr-sovryn.title: Rootstock's Mynt Basket
dllr-sovryn.text: DLLR is Sovryn's BTC-backed dollar basket on Rootstock; reserves are other CDP stables (ZUSD-dominated), readable on-chain. DLLR is Sovryn's Rootstock dollar basket, currently dominated by ZUSD with a small DOC position. The reserve holder can be read on-chain, and the Mynt {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route maps naturally to a basket backstop. The residual risk is not opaque {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, but concentration in Rootstock liquidity, Sovryn governance, and the quality of the underlying BTC-backed stablecoins. Underlying bAssets are themselves {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoins with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} against rBTC.

xusd-babelfish.title: The Rootstock Stablecoin Basket
xusd-babelfish.text:
A Rootstock basket dollar minted 1:1 from bridged stablecoins — a basket exit route, not a fiat-issuer promise, with recursive bridge and dependency risk.

XUSD is BabelFish's Rootstock basket stablecoin, backed by DLLR plus {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} USDT, USDC, DAI, DOC, and related bAssets, with mint and redeem flowing through a basket-level {{term:psm}}PSM-style{{/term}} module. Pharos tracks live branch balances directly from the basket holder and links the largest dependency back to the newly tracked DLLR entry. The model is useful but recursive: XUSD inherits the risks of Rootstock {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} liquidity, DLLR's own basket, and BabelFish's balancing fees. It is a basket exit route, not a fiat issuer promise.

susdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: Savings USDD Wrapper
susdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: sUSDD is a savings wrapper over USDD, which means the first analytical move is not to invent a new peg mechanism. Users deposit USDD, receive a wrapper whose exchange rate appreciates, and ultimately inherit USDD's reserve, PSM, and redemption assumptions on the way out. The wrapper contract itself is comparatively clean, with immutable DSR-style mechanics and no owner or proxy, but the base asset below it is still the load-bearing risk. Pharos records self-reported real-time USDD data, which is useful without being independent reserve assurance. sUSDD is yield passthrough, not alchemy; the wrapper may be tidy, but it cannot launder the parent coin's risk into a different species.

onyc-onre.title: Reinsurance in Stable Drag
onyc-onre.text: ONYC is a Solana NAV token tied to OnRe-managed structured insurance and reinsurance yield, not a plain $1 payment stablecoin with cash in a bank account. Its value is meant to accrue from insurance-market collateral returns, with Apex Group audit coverage and OnRe's Bermuda licensing providing the institutional wrapper. The portfolio is still a single high-risk reserve slice in Pharos because structured reinsurance is not exactly a T-bill ladder with a friendly UI. Primary access remains governed by OnRe's platform terms, and the mint surface runs through an upgradeable Solana program controlled by the issuer. The pitch is yield from a genuinely different real-world market; the catch is that every exit still depends on a high-touch issuer process.

apyusd-apyx.title: Apyx Savings Share
apyusd-apyx.text: apyUSD is the savings wrapper over apxUSD, so the asset is not trying to be the boring cash layer; it is trying to turn Apyx's preferred-share collateral into a rising NAV. The parent reserve stack is the interesting part: Digital Asset Treasury preferred equity and liquidity buffers sit underneath, which is a long way from a plain Treasury-bill stablecoin. Pharos treats the Accountable feed as useful live proof for the wrapper while still carrying the parent dependency and concentrated Apyx admin surface forward. The result is a yield token with a dollar reference and a capital-structure story, which is exactly the sort of thing that looks clean until the collateral thesis has to do real work.

susd1plus-lorenzo.title: Lorenzo Strategy Dollar
susd1plus-lorenzo.text: Lorenzo's staked receipt over the USD1+ strategy dollar, blending WLFI USD1 reserve yield with delta-neutral CEX strategies on BNB Chain. sUSD1+ adds Lorenzo Protocol exposure to the USD1-linked strategy-dollar family. The wrapper is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}}, with returns sourced from {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} positions and CEX strategy access driven by {{term:funding-rate}}funding rate{{/term}} dynamics. Public data supports metadata and supply tracking, but the reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics are less transparent than the cleaner ERC-4626 wrappers, so the entry carries exotic collateral and CEX-strategy {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk.

savusd-avant.title: Avant Staked Dollar
savusd-avant.text: savUSD is Avant's staked avUSD receipt, with the exchange rate rising as the senior tranche earns from actively managed market-neutral strategies. The protection stack is explicit but not magical: Avant points to a Reserve Fund and junior avUSDx tranche before savUSD takes losses, while Pennyworks supplies the weekly NAV calculation. Unstaking has a one-day cooldown with no yield, and the final exit still inherits avUSD's 1:1 USDC redemption process. Pharos therefore reads savUSD as a yield sleeve over a managed strategy book, not as a faster or safer dollar than its parent.

steakusdc-steakhouse.title: Circle, With Borrowers
steakusdc-steakhouse.text: Steakhouse USDC is an immutable MetaMorpho vault share over USDC, so the base dollar is Circle's but the yield comes from borrowers in Steakhouse-curated Morpho markets. That distinction matters: the vault does not improve Circle's reserve story, it adds curator choices, lending collateral, and withdrawal liquidity on top of it. Pharos treats the wrapper minting as deposit-only share accounting while inheriting the underlying USDC issuer risk and tracking the Steakhouse governance surface separately. It is a clean-looking USDC yield wrapper, but exits still depend on available Morpho liquidity; the word "instant" is doing some reputational heavy lifting.

bbqusdc-steakhouse.title: Smokehouse's Higher-Risk USDC Vault
bbqusdc-steakhouse.text: Smokehouse USDC is Steakhouse's high-yield MetaMorpho vault over USDC, built for borrowers and collateral types that sit outside the calmer Prime line. The wrapper still starts with Circle's dollar, but the yield stack is Morpho lending exposure curated toward wider and more exotic collateral markets, including tokenized private-credit style additions. Pharos tracks bbqUSDC as a USDC {{term:yield-bearing}}strategy vault{{/term}}, not a new issuer dollar: share price appreciates through borrower interest, while exits depend on available Morpho liquidity and the curator not having allocated too much into slow-to-unwind markets. The token is transparent and deposit-backed, but the word Smokehouse is doing useful labeling work here; this is the spicy Steakhouse sleeve, not the boring one.

srusde-strata.title: Senior, Not Simple
srusde-strata.text: srUSDe is Strata's senior ERC-4626 tranche over a strategy that stakes USDe into Ethena's yield stack, with jrUSDe taking first-loss before senior holders are touched. That tranche structure is meaningful: it is more disciplined than a naked leveraged loop and gives senior capital a buffer plus a benchmark-rate yield floor. It is still not a plain dollar stablecoin, because exits depend on Strata tranche liquidity and settlement rules rather than a simple 1:1 issuer redemption. Pharos keeps the reserve risk high because the senior wrapper still inherits Ethena's liquid-stablecoin, BTC, ETH/LST, CEX hedge, and custody assumptions. The junior tranche absorbs the first bruise, but if the Ethena machinery breaks badly enough, senior status becomes an adjective, not armor.

syzusd-yuzu.title: Yuzu Staked Wrapper
syzusd-yuzu.text: syzUSD is the staked wrapper for Yuzu USD, so its dollar story begins one layer below the token you are looking at. The wrapper appreciates against yzUSD as curated DeFi strategies accrue yield across Plasma and Monad, while exits inherit Yuzu's KYC-gated redemption and liquidity-buffer constraints. Accountable's real-time reserve feed is the right transparency surface, but Pharos keeps the wrapper identity separate so the same underlying risk is not double-counted as fresh backing. That distinction matters because syzUSD holders are taking strategy-vault risk, parent-coin risk, and young-chain deployment risk in one neat receipt. It is a yield wrapper with accounting discipline; whether that is enough depends on how much comfort one takes from transparent complexity.

fxsave-f-x-protocol.title: f(x) Stability Vault
fxsave-f-x-protocol.text: fxSAVE is an auto-compounding ERC-4626 receipt over f(x) Protocol's Stability Pool, not a simple parked fxUSD balance. The exit path runs through fxSP into a fxUSD-and-USDC mix, then onward into fxUSD's CDP machinery backed by WBTC and wstETH. That gives holders strategy yield and peg-support exposure in one package, but it also imports oracle, liquidation, Curve-pool, and governance-tuned collateral risk. Pharos classifies it as a high-risk NAV strategy vault because the wrapper may look like savings, while the engine underneath is still a leveraged crypto collateral system with better manners.

steakusdt-steakhouse.title: Tether In A Vault
steakusdt-steakhouse.text: Steakhouse USDT is not a new dollar; it is a MetaMorpho vault share over USDT, with yield coming from borrower interest in Steakhouse-curated lending markets. The trust stack is Tether first, Morpho market liquidity second, and Steakhouse curator discipline third, which is quite a lot to fit inside one polite vault receipt. Pharos keeps the Tether issuer and blacklist dependency attached while separately treating the wrapper as a lending vault whose withdrawals rely on available USDT liquidity or patiently returning market capacity. It is a usable yield sleeve, but not a redemption backstop with a steak knife.

susn-noon.title: Noon's Yield Receipt
susn-noon.text: sUSN is the staked savings form of Noon USN, so its NAV appreciates while base USN remains the non-yielding settlement token. The wrapper inherits a reserve mix that is far busier than the name suggests: private credit, CLO exposure, DeFi lending, principal tokens, and a small Treasury-bill sleeve, with Accountable providing a real-time proof feed. That makes sUSN a yield receipt over a credit portfolio, not a fresh $1 stablecoin with its own clean redemption promise. Pharos tracks it separately because wrapper supply, NAV, and liquidity can diverge from liquid USN even though final exits still route through Noon whitelisting and USN reserve constraints. The nice part is transparent wrapper accounting; the less nice part is discovering how many doors sit between savings yield and cash.

mre7yield-midas.title: Midas Re7 Yield Token
mre7yield-midas.text: mRe7YIELD is a Midas and Re7 Capital liquid-yield token, with NAV appreciation sourced from DeFi lending, liquidity provision, restaking, funding-rate trades, and options strategies. That mix may be institutionally packaged, but it is not a cash reserve and should not be mistaken for one because the symbol has a dollar reference. Pharos gives credit for the daily Midas transparency feed while flagging the missing granular strategy-composition feed and the concentrated Midas mint/admin surface. It is a managed strategy note wearing stablecoin colors; useful for yield analytics, awkward as a transactional dollar.

hbusdt-hyperbeat.title: Hyperbeat USDT Vault
hbusdt-hyperbeat.text: hbUSDT is a HyperEVM vault share over USDT strategy exposure, not a cleaner version of Tether with a new logo. Pharos models the reserves as a split between hoUSDT strategy exposure and masterUSD strategy exposure, both high-risk, with Accountable providing real-time visibility that is helpful but still product-scope dependent. The parent leg inherits USDT and USDT0 risk, including Tether redemption discretion and cross-chain settlement assumptions, while the wrapper adds Hyperbeat vault liquidity, strategy allocation, and single-chain HyperEVM execution risk. It is yield-bearing because more machinery was inserted between the holder and the dollar, which is the stablecoin market's favorite magic trick.

witry-brix.title: Wrapped Turkish Lira Yield
witry-brix.text: wiTRY is a Brix staking wrapper over iTRY, exposing holders to a BVI-regulated TRY money-market fund and local Turkish-lira instruments. wiTRY brings a TRY-pegged {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper into the catalog. The Ethereum wrapper can be verified on-chain, while the underlying iTRY reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process remain more issuer-dependent than the mature fiat stablecoin set. The underlying iTRY exposure points at a BVI-regulated TRY money-market structure and local-currency instruments, which Pharos treats as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral with high jurisdictional and operational risk for a thinly traded TRY product.

srusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir Savings Token
srusd-reservoir.text: srUSD is Reservoir's savings wrapper over rUSD, so the immediate asset is a yield-accruing share and the underlying risk is the Reservoir balance sheet. That balance sheet is not a sleepy cash account: it includes stablecoin PSM liquidity, RWA allocations, Morpho and Euler lending vaults, and governance-approved credit strategies. The wrapper adds exchange-rate and exit-to-rUSD mechanics, while rUSD itself still depends on PSM liquidity and protocol risk controls for the actual stablecoin exit. Reservoir's real-time reserve endpoint gives Pharos a live window into the stack, but the window looks into a mixed credit book, not a vault of crisp bills.

usdn-smardex.title: Delta-Neutral USDN
usdn-smardex.text: SMARDEX USDN is the Ethereum synthetic dollar built around a wstETH-backed vault and delta-neutral protocol mechanics, not Noble USDN and blessedly not Neutrino nostalgia. Users mint and redeem through the vault, but the process can be throttled by protocol imbalance and a two-step oracle validation flow, so the peg mechanism is more state machine than cashier window. The token also rebases, which turns yield into a protocol accounting event rather than a separate savings wrapper. Pharos flags the bounded-but-permissioned mint path through the USDN vault and its 2-of-3 governance Safe, because elegant delta-neutral math still needs someone to hold the keys.

scusd-rings.title: Rings Stable Collateral
scusd-rings.text: Rings scUSD is the liquid scAsset, not the main savings wrapper, which is the first useful guardrail before anyone starts annualizing the wrong thing. The collateral model accepts stablecoins and routes a strategy sleeve through Trevee/Veda BoringVault infrastructure into venues such as Aave and Morpho, so the backing is part cash-like collateral and part curated DeFi exposure. Proof is still self-reported through published backing addresses, with Pharos carrying an explicit notice that deeper on-chain reserve tracking is pending. The governance path runs through the Veda/Paladin Safe, timelock, RolesAuthority, and Teller machinery, which is orderly enough to document and centralized enough to matter.

weusd-picwe.title: PicWe USDC Wrapper
weusd-picwe.text: WEUSD is tracked under PicWe (not WEMIX) as a USDC wrapper minted and redeemed 1:1 against USDC, currently trading off-peg near $0.91 despite the documented backing. WEUSD is tracked under PicWe, not WEMIX, because the current documentation and contracts describe PicWe WEUSD. The reserve model is simple today — USDC backing with on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rails — while future {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}/yield collateral stays outside the current scoring assumptions. The off-peg pricing despite documented backing suggests the cross-chain arbitrage loop is not closing efficiently.

gbpe-monerium.title: GBP E-Money Rail
gbpe-monerium.text: GBPe is Monerium's British-pound e-money token, issued under an Icelandic EMI framework rather than a crypto-native collateral game. The reserve story is deliberately dull: safeguarded GBP client funds and permitted EMI reserve assets, with mint and burn handled through KYC'd bank-transfer rails. Pharos still treats the issuer backend and 3-of-6 token-owner Safe as concentrated administration, because regulated does not mean permissionless. For a non-USD stablecoin, that boring bank-rail dependence is the product and the risk; GBPe is useful precisely because it refuses to pretend otherwise.

qcad-stablecorp.title: Regulated CAD Stablecoin
qcad-stablecorp.text: QCAD is a Canadian-dollar stablecoin with the sort of regulatory scaffolding most small fiat tokens can only gesture at: FINTRAC registration, the QCAD Digital Trust framework, and CAD reserves held 1:1 at regulated Canadian institutions. Stablecorp's live balances API gives Pharos real-time supply and reserve totals, which is better than the monthly PDF treasure hunt some issuers still call transparency. The tradeoff is scale and centralization: minting and redemption run through Stablecorp or authorized partners, with Safe-controlled token ownership and upgrade paths rather than permissionless plumbing. For a non-USD stablecoin, QCAD is useful because it is boring in the right places and still small enough that liquidity remains the unglamorous part of the story.

usdxl-last.title: Position-backed synthetic dollar on Hyperliquid
usdxl-last.text: Last USD (USDXL) is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style synthetic dollar minted on HypurrFi (Aave V3 fork on HyperEVM), drawn against HYPE, HYPE LSTs, UBTC, and ETH collateral with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as the only peg defense. Last USD (USDXL) is a crypto-collateralized synthetic dollar minted on HypurrFi, an Aave V3 fork on HyperEVM operated by Last. Users open {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} borrowing positions against HYPE, HYPE LSTs, bridged BTC (UBTC), and ETH, then draw USDXL against that collateral — closer to a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} than to a 1:1 reserve-backed dollar. Repaying the loan burns the synthetic, and undercollateralized positions are hit with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} to defend the peg. Circulating supply sits in the low single-digit millions, with the asset {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}d between Hyperliquid's HyperEVM (18 decimals) and Hyperliquid L1 spot (8 decimals).

bnusd-balanced.title: Balanced's CDP stablecoin extending ICON DeFi cross-chain
bnusd-balanced.text: bnUSD is Balanced's decentralized dollar stablecoin on ICON, minted from {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} against sICX and bridged cross-chain via xCall. BNUSD is the overcollateralized stablecoin of Balanced, a Cosmos/ICON-native lending and DEX protocol. Holders borrow it against sICX (staked ICX) and other Hub collateral on ICON for a 0.2% origination fee plus 2% annualized interest, and the same supply circulates wrapper-free across connected EVM chains and Injective via Balanced's xCall messaging layer. Adding BNUSD gives Pharos coverage of the ICON/Cosmos stablecoin niche — a small but durable ecosystem that no other tracked asset represents — and exposes the cross-chain Hub-issuance pattern as a category. The asset is sub-$5M and currently mid-migration to a v2 design re-anchored on Sonic, so supply and the canonical issuance chain are expected to evolve.

dusd-fluid.title: Banked-cash backing, smart-contract enforced
dusd-fluid.text: DUSD is Fluid Finance's banked-cash USD stablecoin on Arbitrum; self-reported oracle caps mint to safeguarded bank balance. Fluid Finance SA's DigitalDollar is the rare USD stablecoin that holds the float in literal client-safeguarded bank cash — not {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, not commercial paper — at regulated European banks, with theft and fraud cover from Lloyd's of London. The differentiator is the smart-contract verifiedOffchainAssetBalance: an oracle publishes the bank balance to Arbitrum, and the contract refuses to mint DUSD beyond that ceiling. It is the only tracked DUSD that is a single-chain fiat coin, deployed only on Arbitrum at modest ~$3M supply with about 1,000 holders. The structural trade-off is that 'verifiable 24/7' is still self-reported via the issuer's oracle, not an independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and Fluid Finance SA remains a single Swiss entity rather than a regulated bank. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits at regulated European banks and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} burns DUSD on-chain against an IBAN credit.

iusd-initia.title: Initia's AUSD-wrapped ecosystem dollar
iusd-initia.text: Single-chain Initia wrapper of bridged Agora AUSD; reserve yield diverted to ecosystem incentives, redemption routes back through AUSD. iUSD is the native dollar on Initia, the new Move-based Cosmos L1. Each iUSD is backed 1:1 by Agora's AUSD bridged in via LayerZero, so the ultimate reserve trace is Agora's short-dated U.S. Treasuries, repos, and cash custodied at State Street under VanEck management. Unlike standard fiat-backed stables, the reserve yield is redirected by Initia into ecosystem incentives — Echelon lending, liquidity programs, and Cabal vaults — rather than paid to holders. Supply is small (~$4M) and the chain is brand new, so resilience scoring leans on AUSD's transparency rather than an Initia-issued attestation. Holder redemption ultimately routes back through the LayerZero bridge to Agora's USD redemption window. Reserve trace runs into AUSD's {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and cash at State Street with VanEck-managed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with the {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} layer and Agora's {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window owning the exit path.

usdcx-movement.title: Movement's native USDC-backed dollar
usdcx-movement.text: USDCx is Movement's USDC-backed dollar issued via Circle's xReserve smart contract, with CCTP/Gateway {{term:bridge}}bridging{{/term}} to and from USDC across 30+ chains — partner-issued plumbing, not direct Circle paper. USDCx is Movement Network's native dollar stablecoin, launched on M1 mainnet in March 2026 through Circle's xReserve infrastructure. Each USDCx is backed 1:1 by Circle USDC held in a Circle-deployed xReserve smart contract on Movement, and can be moved to USDC across 30+ chains via CCTP and Gateway without third-party {{term:bridge}}bridges{{/term}}. The issuer is Move Industries, the team behind Movement, rather than Circle directly — making USDCx a partner-issued stablecoin whose ultimate solvency inherits from USDC's regulated reserves and Circle {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Circulating supply is still modest (~$2.8M), positioning USDCx as ecosystem rails for Movement-native DeFi, neobank partners like KAST, and Global South payment corridors.

usdh-hubble.title: Solana's original crypto-backed CDP stablecoin, now dormant
usdh-hubble.text: Hubble's USDH was Solana's first MakerDAO-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin at 150% min collateral; today it circulates at ~$1.2-1.5M and is structurally dormant. Hubble Protocol's USDH was the first MakerDAO-style {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} stablecoin on Solana, minted against a basket of SOL, mSOL, BTC, and ETH at a minimum 150% collateralization ratio with Stability Pool {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}. The protocol launched in 2022, raised $5M from Three Arrows, Crypto.com and others, and originally aspired to challenge centralized stablecoin dominance on Solana. Today USDH circulates at roughly $1.2-1.5M with negligible secondary volume, and the team has pivoted its development energy to sister protocol Kamino Finance. No formal sunset has been announced and the borrow app remains live, but USDH is structurally dormant rather than growing. The 'USDH' symbol is shared with Native Markets and Hermetica — three distinct issuers, three distinct collateral models.

zkusd-goal3.title: ZKsync-native sportsbook stablecoin with limited reserve disclosure
zkusd-goal3.text:
A Goal3 sportsbook stable on ZKsync Era, claimed to be overcollateralized but with no itemized backing — treat as venue-restricted credit redeemable through one portal.

zkUSD Dollar is the in-house stable issued by Goal3, a sportsbook on ZKsync Era, with circulating supply just over $1M. Goal3 documents the asset as {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by assets held in the sportsbook, redeemable 1:1 for USDC through the official portal, but the specific accepted collateral, ratios, and on-chain backing addresses are not publicly itemized. Pharos tracks zkUSD primarily for ZKsync ecosystem coverage rather than scale; zkUSD is venue-restricted credit on a single-chain operator, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} access runs through the Goal3 Portal as the only modeled exit. Secondary liquidity exists on SyncSwap and a small MEXC listing.

ist-agoric.title: Cosmos-native crypto-backed stable with sub-$5M strategic coverage
ist-agoric.text: Agoric's overcollateralized dollar minted from IBC ATOM/stATOM vaults with a PSM for 1:1 IBC stablecoin swaps; tiny strategic Cosmos coverage. Inter Stable Token (IST) is the Agoric platform's native fee token and an overcollateralized crypto-backed stablecoin governed via Inter Protocol. IST is minted two ways: through vault positions collateralized by IBC-bridged ATOM and stATOM with a stability fee and Dutch-auction liquidations, and through a Parity Stability Module (PSM) that swaps approved IBC stablecoins (USDC, USDT, DAI) for IST 1:1. Total circulating supply is ~$1.4M across Agoric native, Osmosis, Archway, and Secret Network deployments — well below Pharos's $5M soft threshold, but tracked as a strategic Cosmos-ecosystem entry where overcollateralized fiat-pegged designs remain rare. Pharos uses DefiLlama as the primary supply feed; coverage today reflects the Osmosis IBC slice only until upstream tracking broadens to Agoric native. The design is a textbook {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, Dutch-auction {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, and an IBC-stablecoin {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} as the peg backstop.

benji-franklin-templeton.title: The Onchain '40 Act Money Market Fund
benji-franklin-templeton.text: BENJI is the on-chain share token for Franklin Templeton's FOBXX, an SEC-registered U.S. government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a stable $1.00 NAV. BENJI is Franklin Templeton's tokenised share class of FOBXX, the Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund — a Securities Act of 1933 and Investment Company Act of 1940 registered money market fund custodied at BNY Mellon. The token holds a stable $1.00 NAV; yield is distributed by rebasing the holder's share count on-chain rather than letting the price drift, which makes BENJI behave like a par-redeemable dollar even though it is legally a fund share. With roughly $2 billion in assets across Stellar (primary), Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Aptos, Base, Solana, BNB Chain, Canton, and Ethereum, it is the largest tokenised '40 Act {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} in market. Pharos currently tracks the Ethereum supply contract and runs reserves on a curated weekly snapshot of the official Franklin Templeton factsheet pending per-chain verification and oracle availability.

wtgxx-wisdomtree.title: WisdomTree's 24/7 Dealer-Traded Treasury Fund
wtgxx-wisdomtree.text:
A SEC-approved tokenized government MMF trading at a fixed $1 NAV 24/7 through WisdomTree Connect dealers, with $857M across seven chains.

WTGXX is the digital share class of WisdomTree's Government Money Market Digital Fund, a '40 Act-registered {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} that received SEC approval in early 2026 to support 24/7 dealer trading at a fixed $1.00 NAV — making it one of the most stable-coin-like tokenised MMFs in market. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} are gated to WisdomTree Connect users with USDC dealer settlement and USD-wire alternatives; holdings are short-duration U.S. government obligations ({{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}), repos, and cash as the {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}} backing. Around $857 million of AUM sits across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, Optimism, Plume, and Stellar; Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first and runs a curated weekly snapshot of the official WisdomTree fund factsheet for reserves.

vbill-vaneck.title: VanEck's Securitize-Administered Treasury Share
vbill-vaneck.text: VBILL is the on-chain share token for VanEck's Treasury Fund, with Van Eck advising the BVI Professional Fund and Securitize handling administration, tokenization, transfer agency, and KYC. The reserve stack is pleasantly dull: mostly short-duration U.S. T-bills with a cash and repo sleeve, while the token itself accrues NAV rather than rebasing balances. Primary mint and redemption run through Securitize Markets against USDC, AUSD, or wire rails, and the multi-chain footprint is bridged rather than a free-for-all native issuance set. Pharos tracks the live NAV path through the Chainlink NAVLink feed and keeps the product framed as an institutional Treasury share, not a par retail stablecoin. VBILL is the kind of tokenized fund where the boring assets are the feature and the wrapper paperwork is the hobby.

acred-apollo-securitize.title: Private Credit, Not Treasuries
acred-apollo-securitize.text: ACRED is a tokenized, NAV-accreting feeder share into Apollo's diversified private credit fund — backing is illiquid private credit, not T-bills, so the risk profile is medium-to-high rather than cash-like. ACRED is the on-chain feeder share into Apollo Diversified Credit Fund, a multi-strategy private credit portfolio combining direct lending, structured credit, performing credit, and dislocated credit. Unlike BUIDL or BENJI, the collateral is illiquid private credit rather than {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} — risk profile is medium-to-high and closer to syrupUSDC than to a stable-NAV vehicle. ACRED is NAV-accreting; primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is monthly at fund NAV through Securitize Markets, supplemented by an on-demand liquidity pool sized to roughly 5% of NAV, and RedStone publishes a NAV oracle used by integrations. Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract and flags this asset as a private-credit NAV token rather than a par stablecoin.

eutbl-spiko.title: Europe's First Tokenised T-Bill MMF
eutbl-spiko.text: EUTBL is Spiko's AMF-regulated UCITS short-term {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} backed by Eurozone {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} — Europe's first tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} sovereign fund. EUTBL is Spiko's EUR-denominated short-term money market fund — the first AMF-regulated UCITS MMF tokenised on Ethereum. The fund holds short-dated Eurozone sovereign T-bills with weighted average maturity under two months, and EUTBL behaves as a VNAV (variable-NAV) share that accretes value as T-bill yield compounds. Primary subscriptions and redemptions settle same-day at fund NAV with a €1k minimum; Chainlink CCIP bridges issuance to Arbitrum and Polygon. EUTBL is one of Pharos's few EUR-pegged RWA assets and one of the cleanest fits for European institutional users seeking regulatory-grade tokenised cash — a fit that got materially easier to access in June, when Coinbase opened stablecoin-funded subscriptions and redemptions for Spiko's UCITS funds settling on Base.

ustbl-spiko.title: Spiko's USD T-Bill MMF Cousin
ustbl-spiko.text: USTBL is Spiko's USD-denominated AMF-regulated UCITS {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} holding short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, deployed across Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Polygon via Chainlink CCIP. USTBL is the USD-denominated sister fund to Spiko's EUTBL — same AMF-regulated UCITS {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} architecture, same ERC-1967 upgradeable proxy, same Chainlink CCIP multi-chain rollout (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon), but holding short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills instead of Eurozone sovereigns. The VNAV share accretes value as T-bill yield compounds, with $1k minimums and same-day NAV settlement. Backed by {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and AMF {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, USTBL behaves as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share rather than a par stablecoin. The combined Spiko AUM passed $1 billion in late 2025, making the pair one of the larger EU-regulated tokenised treasury franchises in market. Distribution took its biggest step yet in June, when Coinbase opened USDC and EURC subscriptions and redemptions for Spiko's UCITS funds settling on Base — EU-regulated money-market shares, one tap from an exchange balance.

jtrsy-anemoy.title: S&P's Highest-Rated Tokenised Fund
jtrsy-anemoy.text: BVI Professional Fund holding short-duration U.S. T-bills via Centrifuge ERC-7540; AA+f / S1+ S&P rating, NAV settlement for whitelisted professionals. JTRSY is the Janus Henderson Anemoy Treasury Fund, a BVI Professional Fund where Janus Henderson acts as sub-advisor and Centrifuge handles the on-chain ERC-7540 vault. The fund is rated AA+f / S1+ by S&P, currently the highest credit rating assigned to any tokenised fund. Holdings are short-duration U.S. T-bills; primary subscriptions and redemptions settle same-day at fund NAV for whitelisted non-U.S. Professional Investors via Centrifuge's issuer rail. Distribution extends across Centrifuge V3 to additional chains; Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first, with reserve data curated until Centrifuge's on-chain NAV publishing path is available for automated reserve verification. Holdings are pure short-duration {{term:treasury}}U.S. T-bills{{/term}} held as a tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share with permissioned Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and same-day NAV {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}.

bib01-backed.title: Backed's Flagship Treasury Tracker
bib01-backed.text: bIB01 is Backed's NAV-accreting tracker token for the BlackRock iShares 0-1 year U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury Bond{{/term}} UCITS ETF, KYC-gated under Swiss DLT Act framework — not pegged to $1. bIB01 is Backed Finance's most-traded tokenised {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} ETF: a Swiss DLT Act-registered tracker certificate that fully backs each token with the BlackRock iShares $ Treasury Bond 0-1yr UCITS ETF (IB01). The token is NAV-accreting and not pegged to $1 — price drifts upward continuously as the underlying T-bill ETF accrues yield. Primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are KYC-gated through Backed; secondary liquidity is on Uniswap and CoW Protocol. bIB01 deploys on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Gnosis, and Avalanche using the same contract address pattern that Backed uses across its product line.

bc3m-backed.title: Backed's EUR Govt Bond Tracker
bc3m-backed.text: bC3M is Backed's NAV-accreting tracker token for Amundi's short-dated Eurozone government bond UCITS ETF, KYC-gated and registered under Swiss DLT Act — one of the few EUR-pegged {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} tokens. bC3M is Backed Finance's EUR-denominated tokenised tracker certificate fully backed by the AMUNDI GOVIES 0-6 Months Euro Investment Grade UCITS ETF. The token is NAV-accreting in euros, giving Pharos one of the few EUR-pegged RWA assets backed by short-duration Eurozone government bonds — economically the EUR analogue of a {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bond{{/term}} tracker. Same Swiss DLT Act framework as bIB01, same KYC-gated primary issuance through Backed and KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, same Uniswap / CoW secondary liquidity surfaces. Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first; Backed also publishes the asset on Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis using its multi-chain deployment pattern.

ntbill-nest.title: Nest's On-Plume Treasury Vault
ntbill-nest.text: Nest Credit Treasury vault share on Plume routing into Superstate USTB/USCC and Janus Henderson JTRSY; NAV-accreting fund-of-funds-style token, not a par-redeemable dollar. nTBILL is Nest Credit's {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} vault on Plume: a vault share whose value tracks a curated book of Superstate USTB / USCC and Janus Henderson JTRSY positions, plus a small stablecoin liquidity buffer. The token is NAV-accreting and primary mint/{{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} runs through Nest at vault NAV. Reserves are sourced live from the Nest Credit positions API, the same positions source that supports inALPHA. Pharos tracks nTBILL because it references a dollar base, but the token behaves like a tokenised {{term:money-market-fund}}fund-of-funds{{/term}} share rather than a par-redeemable stablecoin.

nbasis-nest.title: Nest's Basis-Trade Vault
nbasis-nest.text: Nest Credit basis-trade vault token combining tokenized T-bill collateral with perpetual shorts; NAV-accreting rather than $1-pegged, value drifts with funding-rate performance. nBASIS is Nest Credit's {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} strategy vault: tokenised {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} collateral combined with {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} short positions, rebalanced by Nest. Closer in profile to Ethena USDe or Midas mRe7YIELD than to a par stablecoin — the token's value drifts with {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} performance rather than holding $1. Pharos lists it because the strategy references the dollar as its base and the Nest Credit positions API publishes live NAV, but the methodology treats nBASIS as a strategy vault with high collateral-quality risk and a NAV-token notice.

nopal-nest.title: Nest's BlackOpal Credit Vault
nopal-nest.text: Nest Credit vault token wrapping BlackOpal LiquidStone II tokenized private-credit positions plus a small liquidity buffer; NAV-accreting vault share, not a par-redeemable stablecoin. nOPAL is Nest Credit's BlackOpal LiquidStone II vault: tokenised private-credit positions plus a small {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} and stablecoin liquidity buffer. Like other Nest vaults, the token is NAV-accreting and primary access runs through Nest at vault NAV. Pharos flags nOPAL as a private-credit vault share rather than a par stablecoin; the high-risk reserve slice reflects the underlying LiquidStone II credit positions classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent exposure.

nwisdom-nest.title: Nest's WisdomTree-Backed Vault
nwisdom-nest.text: Nest Credit vault share built around WisdomTree Connect tokenized fund exposure (xCRDYX) plus an nTBILL liquidity buffer; NAV-accreting tokenized fund share, not a par stablecoin. nWISDOM is Nest Credit's vault built around WisdomTree's tokenised fund shares (xCRDYX and related WisdomTree Connect products) with a small nTBILL and stablecoin liquidity buffer, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent vault exposure. Yield accretes through the underlying WisdomTree fund NAV; primary mint/{{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} runs through Nest at vault NAV. Pharos tracks it on the same live reserves pattern as inALPHA, with the understanding that the token is a vault share rather than a par stablecoin.

susdc-spark.title: Spark's USDC share class on the Sky savings rate
susdc-spark.text: Spark Savings USDC is an ERC-4626 savings wrapper that lets USDC holders access the Sky Savings Rate without manually converting into USDS first. Deposits route through Spark's PSM and savings machinery, so the share price appreciates against USDC while the base exposure still inherits Circle issuer risk and Sky governance's rate-setting authority. The vault withdrawal path is on-chain, but final USDC liquidity still depends on Spark and PSM liquidity being available when holders want out. Pharos treats spUSDC as a savings-passthrough wrapper rather than a new reserve design, which is the only sane way to read one protocol's yield plumbing wrapped around another issuer's dollar. It is convenient, not independent.

susdt-spark.title: USDT-denominated Spark Savings vault on the Sky rate
susdt-spark.text: Spark Savings USDT is the Tether-denominated version of Spark's savings passthrough into the Sky Savings Rate. The wrapper gives USDT holders a rising share price, but the risk stack is not just Spark: it inherits Tether issuer exposure, Spark vault mechanics, Sky governance rate decisions, and whatever liquidity the vault and PSM can actually supply on withdrawal. That is a lot of institutional and protocol trust to package as one tidy ERC-4626 receipt. Pharos treats spUSDT separately from spUSDC because changing the underlying issuer changes the dependency surface, even if the vault interface looks nearly identical. Same savings plumbing, different centralized dollar underneath.

sgho-aave.title: Aave's non-slashable GHO savings module
sgho-aave.text:
Aave's non-slashable GHO yield product — 1:1 deposits, governance-set savings rate, no cooldown — separate from the slashable Umbrella stkGHO safety module.

Aave Savings GHO (sGHO) is the non-slashable GHO {{term:yield-bearing}}yield product{{/term}} offered alongside the slashable Umbrella stkGHO safety module. Depositors mint sGHO against GHO at a 1:1 conversion and receive GHO-denominated emissions at the Aave-governance-set savings rate. The module holds a nine-figure pile of GHO and pays out without cooldown or slashing risk; it is distinct from the Umbrella stkGHO position that absorbs deficit events for the GHO market, and underneath sits GHO's own {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral profile. Yield is governance-set, so emissions can move with Aave DAO decisions.

gtusdcp-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's curated USDC MetaMorpho V2 vault
gtusdcp-gauntlet.text: Gauntlet USDC Prime is a MetaMorpho V2 vault that turns USDC into a curated lending exposure across permissioned Morpho Blue markets. The wrapper is immutable and deposit-backed, but the risk is actively curated: Gauntlet sets and updates allocations across markets backed by blue-chip crypto, RWA, and yield-bearing collateral. Share price appreciation comes from borrower interest, while withdrawals depend on available Morpho liquidity and the curator not having optimized the portfolio into a queue at the wrong moment. Pharos tracks it as a USDC strategy vault, not a new stablecoin, because the base dollar risk still rolls back to Circle and the lending-book risk belongs to Morpho allocation. The vault is professional enough to be useful and composable enough to be dangerous in all the usual ways.

gtusdc-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's conservative USDC MetaMorpho vault
gtusdc-gauntlet.text: gtUSDC is a Gauntlet-curated MetaMorpho V1 USDC vault, an ERC-4626 wrapper compounding {{term:yield-bearing}}lending yield{{/term}} across vetted Morpho Blue markets on Ethereum. Gauntlet USDC Prime V1 (gtUSDC) is the Ethereum-only V1 Morpho Prime vault curated by Gauntlet — a $145M MetaMorpho deployment across vetted USDC lending markets on Morpho Blue, distinct from the separately tracked Prime V2 vault (gtusdcp-gauntlet) at a different contract address. Share price appreciates against USDC as borrower interest accrues, with withdrawals dependent on borrower {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} flow and Morpho market depth. Tracking the V1 and V2 vaults as separate entries exists for the same reason Pharos tracks Steakhouse USDC and Steakhouse USDT separately — distinct curated portfolios warrant their own risk telemetry.

yvusdc-yearn.title: Yearn v3's aggregator USDC vault
yvusdc-yearn.text:
Canonical Yearn v3 USDC vault routing through Aave, Compound, Morpho, and Sky; ~$30M Ethereum AUM with queue-based withdrawals and centralized strategy selection.

yvUSDC-1 is the canonical Yearn v3 USDC vault: an ERC-4626 {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share token whose price appreciates against USDC as Yearn's strategy allocator rotates underlying capital across whitelisted yield strategies (Aave, Compound, Morpho, Sky, and similar). The Ethereum vault holds about $30M of USDC. {{term:redemption}}Withdrawals{{/term}} route through Yearn v3's queue and depend on aggregate strategy liquidity; centralised strategy selection sits with Yearn governance.

aa-falconx-mev-capital.title: FalconX Credit Vault
aa-falconx-mev-capital.text: AA_FalconXUSDC is a Pareto credit-vault tranche, not a Falcon Finance stablecoin and not a MEV Capital strategy token despite the naming fog. The underlying exposure is USDC deployed into FalconX institutional credit lines curated by M11 Credit, so the risk is private-credit performance and redemption timing rather than peg arbitrage. Pharos treats it as a yield-bearing NAV token because monthly exits and vault accounting are the product, not incidental details. The on-chain tranche cannot mint itself independently of the IdleCDO deposit path, which is good plumbing but not a credit guarantee. Distribution is scaling up around it — Plume's new FALX facility now routes on-chain capital into the same FalconX credit book, with ambitions toward a billion dollars of capacity. This is stablecoin infrastructure being used to tokenize a lender's balance-sheet slice, and the word 'USDC' in the symbol should not lull anyone into reading it as cash.

vndc-jade-labs.title: Vietnam's most-trafficked VND stablecoin with weak attestation
vndc-jade-labs.text: VNDC is Jade Labs's Vietnamese dong stablecoin redeemable 1:1 via ONUS and VNDC Hub, with self-reported reserves and no independent attestation cadence. VNDC is a Vietnamese dong-pegged stablecoin issued by Jade Labs (the company behind ONUS Finance), the only credible on-chain VND instrument with material market presence. The issuer self-reports 1:1 fiat backing with VND {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Vietnamese banking partners and operates mint/redemption flows through those partners and the ONUS app, but no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence is published and aggregator-reported market cap has historically diverged from observable on-chain Polygon and BSC supply. Pharos lists VNDC across Polygon and BNB Smart Chain at zero decimals (the contracts mint whole-unit VNDC); the issuer's third ONUS-chain deployment is not in scope until that chain is tracked. The detail page carries an explicit attestation warning so users do not infer the reported $50M aggregate as fully verifiable.

mmxn-moneta-digital.title: Mexico's Self-Reported MXN Stablecoin
mmxn-moneta-digital.text: MMXN is Moneta Digital's peso stablecoin, backed by issuer-reported MXN bank reserves rather than a current independent attestation cadence. The metadata supports Ethereum and Tron deployments, while Pharos deliberately keeps other historical chain claims out of the curated set until official confirmation catches up with explorer archaeology. The reserve disclosure mentions Delchain and Deltec custody context and an old Armanino engagement, but the live proof path today is still self-reported and ad hoc. Mint authority is also bluntly centralized, with issuer-controlled EOAs confirmed as minters on both tracked chains. MMXN may be useful peso rails, but compared with better-attested local-currency peers, it asks users to accept a lot of 'trust us' in a market that has already seen that movie.

hkdr-rd-technologies.title: Missed the First Wave, Still in the Race
hkdr-rd-technologies.text: Pre-launch HKD stablecoin from RD Technologies; in HKMA sandbox but missed the April 2026 first licence cohort. HKDR is the HKD stablecoin from RD Technologies, a Hong Kong fintech founded by former HKMA chief executive Norman Chan. Its subsidiary RD InnoTech was in the first July 2024 cohort admitted to the HKMA stablecoin issuer sandbox — testing digital-asset trading rails and cross-border trade payments — and the firm has been positioning for licensing under the Stablecoins Ordinance that took effect August 1 2025. On 2026-04-10 the HKMA gazetted the first stablecoin issuer licences (FRS01 and FRS02) to Anchorpoint and HSBC, with RD InnoTech absent from that cohort. RD remains a credible later-license contender — a recent Series A2 round and a memorandum of understanding with ZA Bank both point to a serious operational build-out — but the regulatory window has shifted to a slower queue. The entry remains pre-launch until licence issuance is confirmed. The eventual product still routes through HKMA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a regulated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window.

brd-volpon.title: Selic-Linked Yield, In a Token
brd-volpon.text: BRD is a pre-launch Brazilian real stablecoin from CF Inovacao, backed by Brazilian {{term:treasury}}Treasury bonds{{/term}} and structured to pass Selic-rate yield back to holders. BRD is a BRL stablecoin announced January 6 2026 by Tony Volpon, a former deputy governor of the Central Bank of Brazil, through his company CF Inovacao. The distinctive structural choice: BRD is backed by Brazilian National Treasury bonds and explicitly designed to pass the Selic-linked yield (currently around 15%) back to holders, rather than retaining it as issuer revenue. That is the same model Crown's BRLV already operates in institutional channels — Crown raised $13.5M from Paradigm in December 2025 — but BRD is positioning as the first to make {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-sharing{{/term}} the primary product framing rather than a niche feature. The competitive set in Brazilian BRL stablecoins is small but real: Transfero BRZ ($185M), BBRL ($51M), BRL1, plus cREAL on Celo. The harder gate is Brazilian regulation: BCB's FX-classification regime took effect February 2 2026 and final Consulta Publica 111 output is still pending, which is why Volpon has not published a launch date alongside the announcement.

krw1-bdacs.title: Korea's First Bank-Backed Won Stablecoin, Stuck in PoC
krw1-bdacs.text: BDACS/Woori KRW PoC on Avalanche with real-time banking-API reserve attestation; commercial gating awaits Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act. KRW1 is BDACS's KRW-backed stablecoin, developed with Woori Bank as the reserve custodian and launched on Avalanche in September 2025 — but in a proof-of-concept phase, not in public circulation. The structural advantages are real: real-time banking-API reserve attestation through Woori, KISA's endorsement of Avalanche for public-sector reliability, and a February 2026 Plume partnership that positions KRW1 as the Korean institutional settlement rail for tokenized RWAs (Plume hosts roughly $645M in tokenized assets). The commercial gating is Korea's still-pending Digital Asset Basic Act framework, where BDACS is explicitly trying to make KRW1 the technical standard. The strategic weakness is distribution — BDACS is a B2B custodian without a consumer app or retail footprint, which makes KRW1 likely to win on the institutional side and lose to bank-led or super-app issuers if Korea's eventual framework favours retail surfaces. Real-time banking-API {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} runs through Woori Bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with KRW1 positioning itself as the settlement rail for Korean institutional {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} flows and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} routed through regulated banking channels.

rusd-revolut.title: The Cyprus Licence Was the Easy Part
rusd-revolut.text: Revolut's expected USD stablecoin remains pre-launch, with ticker, chain, and reserve model still unannounced. RUSD represents Revolut's expected USD stablecoin direction, sister to the already-tracked RGBP. The legal substrate was assembled in 2025: Revolut Digital Assets Europe took a MiCA CASP licence from CySEC on October 23 2025, and Revolut's existing Bank-of-Lithuania EMI provides the e-money-token issuer foundation that MiCA Title IV requires. The Cyprus announcement also unveiled 'Crypto 2.0' with '1:1 conversion between stablecoins and USD' as a flagship feature — close enough to a product tease that EU counsel described a 2026 Revolut stablecoin as plausible. The harder questions are downstream: ticker, chain choice, reserve and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} disclosure model, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics, and how Revolut navigates the UK Bank of England's proposed restrictions on cross-group stablecoin issuance that already constrain RGBP. Ticker, chain, reserve model, and first-issued variant remain unannounced.

brl-itau.title: Brazil's Biggest Bank Waits for the Rulebook
brl-itau.text: BRL-ITAU is a pre-launch stablecoin under evaluation by Brazil's largest private bank Itau Unibanco, with peg currency and design pending BCB regulation. Itau Unibanco — Brazil's largest private bank by assets — confirmed in April 2025 that it is evaluating its own stablecoin, with Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes telling a Sao Paulo industry event the bank is 'always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. The peg-currency choice (BRL or USD) is explicitly undecided and gated on the final shape of Brazil's regulatory framework via BCB Consulta Publica 111, especially the open self-{{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} question that Antunes flagged as a major design constraint. Itau already participates in the DREX wholesale CBDC pilot, providing distribution-rail experience but also a competing institutional product that may shape final positioning; primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} would presumably run through Itau's bank network. The placeholder is BRL-denominated because Brazil's retail base and Itau's franchise make a real-denominated launch the most likely first design, while Itau has not ruled out a USD-denominated option.

usd-nubank.title: Stablecoins Strapped to the Credit Card
usd-nubank.text: Nubank's USD stablecoin row is still pre-launch, but it is structurally interesting because the proposed surface is credit-card payments rather than a DeFi wallet. Roberto Campos Neto framed the pilot as part of a broader Nubank push into tokenized deposits and credit against tokenized assets, which is a much larger ambition than adding another dollar balance to an app. The unresolved question remains whether Nubank issues its own dollar token or routes through a third-party stablecoin such as USDC or PYUSD, and that answer decides the custody, reserve, and redemption model. Pharos keeps the placeholder as centralized and regulated-entity-driven because a Nubank rail would almost certainly be permissioned even if the token touches public chains later. The asset here is not the ticker; it is Nubank's distribution across Latin America, which is exactly why the missing product details matter.

moveusd-cfx.title: CFX's Solana Deposit Dollar
moveusd-cfx.text: CFX-issued tokenized-deposit dollar on Solana, roughly $120M circulating against USD deposits, cash equivalents, and U.S. Treasuries; no independent reserve feed is public yet. MoveUSD is a CFX-issued dollar settlement instrument with DefiLlama reporting roughly $120M in circulating supply and a live Solana price path. The token is best read as tokenized-deposit infrastructure rather than a permissionless DeFi-native stablecoin: minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through the issuer, while the SPL mint gives Pharos a concrete on-chain supply anchor. Reserves are described as USD deposits, cash equivalents, and marketable U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} securities, but no independently audited reserve feed is public yet. The detail page carries a tokenized-deposit caveat so users do not confuse the high market cap with open retail redemption coverage.

hlusd-hela.title: HeLa's Native Runtime Dollar
hlusd-hela.text: Centralized USD stablecoin for the HeLa chain; CoinGecko-only coverage, no contract-level reserve telemetry yet. HLUSD is the native dollar stablecoin for the HeLa ecosystem, admitted through CoinGecko because the HeLa chain is not yet a supported Pharos contract platform. CoinGecko reports a positive price and market cap, but contract-level supply and issuer reserve telemetry remain outside the supported chain set. The asset is therefore classified as a centralized-dependent RWA-backed USD coin with an explicit unsupported-chain notice. The unusually high trading volume relative to supply makes it useful coverage, while HeLa chain support and stronger reserve documentation remain the main open data gaps. Until the issuer publishes a verifiable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and discloses {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path remains the dominant unknown.

xmd-metal-dollar.title: A Stablecoin Basket on XPR Network
xmd-metal-dollar.text:
Metallicus's basket dollar wraps USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar exposure on XPR Network — convenient as an index, hard to verify outside CoinGecko.

Metal Dollar is a basket-backed dollar token on XPR Network, with public materials pointing to USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar components as the reserve set held in issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Pharos admits it through CoinGecko's price and market-cap path because XPR Network is not currently supported for contract coverage. The structure gives XMD upstream exposure to centralized stablecoin issuers while leaving direct holder-control semantics hard to verify from Pharos' chain set, and no public {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed itemizes the basket weights. It is useful basket-stablecoin coverage, but Pharos keeps dependency weights coarse until reserve composition and redemption depth are disclosed more granularly.

vusd-virtue.title: IOTA-Backed CDP Dollar
vusd-virtue.text: Virtue USD is an IOTA-ecosystem {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin backed by IOTA and stIOTA positions, with high-risk collateral and IOTA not yet a Pharos-supported chain. Virtue USD is an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} IOTA ecosystem stablecoin backed by IOTA and stIOTA positions, with {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as peg defense. CoinGecko resolves the IOTA object and reports a positive market cap, but IOTA itself is not yet a Pharos-supported chain, so the registry intentionally excludes contracts for now. That means Pharos can show price, market-cap, and risk metadata, while on-chain supply, mint/burn, and contract authority analysis remain future work. The collateral profile is high-risk compared with fiat-backed stablecoins because peg defense ultimately depends on volatile IOTA-family collateral and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics.

stusd-stoneyield.title: A Yield Wrapper Wearing a Dollar Label
stusd-stoneyield.text: StoneYield USD is a BNB Chain yield wrapper over USDC and Venus-linked strategy positions, not a plain fiat dollar with a bank account behind it. The reserve model points to USDC routed through StoneYield's managed protocol layer, so stability depends on both the underlying stablecoin and the strategy wrapper doing what it says on the label. Pharos marks stUSD as yield-bearing and NAV-style because the holder is accepting vault mechanics, admin controls, and withdrawal liquidity risk in exchange for the yield path. CoinGecko can provide the market row, but a stronger independent APY and reserve feed would make the entry less dependent on issuer-side framing. It is a dollar wrapper in the same way a structured note is cash: close enough for marketing, not close enough for risk.

lvusd-leverup.title: Monad Perps Collateral in Stablecoin Form
lvusd-leverup.text: Small Monad-based stable asset tied to LeverUp's perpetuals engine, not a cash-backed issuer dollar; redemption and reserve depth depend on a trading system rather than a bank balance sheet. LeverUp USD is a small Monad stablecoin tied to LeverUp's liquidity layer for perpetuals and margin trading. CoinGecko reports a live price and market cap, and the Monad contract is included because Pharos already has a Monad chain entry. The risk profile is not comparable to a cash-backed issuer coin: collateral and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are tied to a trading engine that references USDC and MON, and public reserve depth is still thin. Pharos therefore treats lvUSD as a notice-heavy crypto-backed stable asset rather than a conventional dollar reserve token.

nusd-nexus.title: Legacy Synapse Bridge Liquidity
nusd-nexus.text: Legacy Synapse bridge-liquidity stable asset backed by a DAI/USDC/USDT pool; closer to bridge routing infrastructure than a standalone modern issuer, with inherited freezability and dependency risk. Nexus USD is a legacy Synapse {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}-liquidity stable asset backed by a pool of DAI, USDC, and USDT. It is included because DefiLlama still returns both a current price and circulating supply, but the product model is closer to bridge routing infrastructure than to a standalone modern issuer. The upstream reserve basket gives NUSD inherited freezability and stablecoin dependency risk. Contract coverage is intentionally omitted until the active Synapse deployment set is freshly verified across chains.

brlm-mento.title: Mento's Brazilian Real Rail
brlm-mento.text: BRLm is Mento's oracle-priced Brazilian real on Celo, exchanged through FPMM swap routes against the diversified {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. BRLm expands Mento coverage into Brazilian real-denominated settlement on Celo. Unlike the existing Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} rows, this entry uses the reserve-wide Mento dashboard feed because the current CDP trove API only covers GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm. The reserve mix is diversified but still exposed to sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, USDT, axlEUROC, stETH, and smaller assets, so Pharos classifies collateral quality as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade. BRLm is small in absolute supply, but strategically useful because it adds another BRL rail from an already-modeled issuer family.

phpm-mento.title: PUSO Joins the PHP Set
phpm-mento.text:
Mento's Celo-native Philippine peso stablecoin uses the shared Mento reserve basket rather than PHP bank deposits, completing Pharos's regional PHP coverage.

PHPm, marketed by Mento as PUSO, is a Celo-based Philippine peso stablecoin with live DefiLlama price and circulating-supply coverage. It uses Mento's oracle-priced swap and reserve architecture rather than a bank-deposit PHP reserve, so the collateral stack is the same mixed Mento reserve basket used across the reserve-backed Mento family. Pharos already tracks other PHP-pegged issuers, making PHPm useful for ecosystem completion and regional coverage. The live reserve feed is shared with the broader Mento reserve dashboard rather than a PHPm-specific {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}.

kesm-mento.title: First Kenyan Shilling Stablecoin Coverage
kesm-mento.text: First Kenyan shilling stable in Pharos; runs on Celo via Mento's reserve-backed FX mechanism, grouped under OTHER until KES has a dedicated peg category. KESm is the first Kenyan shilling-denominated stable asset in Pharos, admitted through DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply path. The token runs on Celo and uses the same Mento reserve-backed FX mechanism as the newer Mento local-currency suite. Because KES does not yet have a dedicated Pharos peg category, the asset is grouped under OTHER. The reserve risk remains driven by the Mento mix, especially CELO exposure and upstream centralized stablecoins. Mechanically KESm is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style Mento FX stablecoin with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} against the multi-asset reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via FPMM swaps at oracle-driven rates.

copm-mento.title: Colombian Peso Coverage via Celo
copm-mento.text: COPm is Mento's oracle-priced Colombian peso stablecoin on Celo; first COP reference on Pharos. COPm adds Colombian peso stablecoin coverage through Mento's Celo deployment. DefiLlama supplies price and circulating-value data, while the contract is verified from the Celo token-contract table. COP is grouped under OTHER rather than a dedicated peg category. The addition is small-cap but useful because it gives the dashboard a first Colombian peso reference. The reserve relies on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} across a mixed crypto and stablecoin basket and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps.

cadm-mento.title: A Tiny CAD Rail from Mento
cadm-mento.text: CADm is Mento's oracle-priced CAD stablecoin on Celo, backed by the shared Mento reserve rather than Canadian bank reserves. CADm is Mento's Canadian dollar stable asset on Celo, added mainly for ecosystem completion rather than market size. DefiLlama provides price and supply coverage, and the token uses a verified Celo contract, but circulating supply remains tiny compared with larger CAD stablecoin issuers already tracked by Pharos. The collateral story is Mento reserve exposure rather than Canadian-dollar bank reserves. That means resilience depends on Celo, Mento governance, and the mixed reserve basket behind the broader Mento system. The reserve relies on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} across a basket of stablecoins and crypto, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps rather than fiat off-ramps.

audm-mento.title: Mento's AUD Completes Another Local Rail
audm-mento.text: AUDm is Mento's crypto-backed Australian dollar on Celo, minted by depositing USDm as Liquity-v2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral against the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. AUDm is the Mento Australian dollar asset on Celo, distinct from the already tracked Macropod AUDM despite the shared ticker style. It is admitted through DefiLlama and a verified Celo contract, with live reserve visibility through the shared Mento dashboard. The supply is small, so the value is mainly comparative: users can now see Mento's AUD rail beside larger AUD issuers and the rest of the Mento FX set. Reserves remain mixed and on-chain rather than an Australian-dollar banking stack.

ghsm-mento.title: Ghanaian Cedi Coverage, Grouped as Other
ghsm-mento.text: GHSm is Mento's Celo Ghanaian cedi stablecoin backed by a mixed reserve (sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, stETH) — small-supply currency coverage rather than a market signal. GHSm brings Ghanaian cedi exposure into Pharos through Mento's Celo stablecoin suite. DefiLlama provides price and supply data, while CoinGecko's active slug resolves as cGHS rather than the stale DefiLlama gecko hint. Like KESm and COPm, GHSm is grouped under OTHER because GHS does not yet have a dedicated peg category. It is very small, but it extends coverage into a currency region otherwise missing from the dashboard, with backing tied to Mento's shared {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} reserve and on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flows.

zarm-mento.title: Mento's Smaller ZAR Stablecoin
zarm-mento.text:
Celo-issued ZAR stable from Mento's local-currency program, inheriting reserve risk from the shared Mento mix rather than ZAR bank collateral.

ZARm is a Celo-based South African rand stable asset from Mento minted {{term:cdp}}CDP-style{{/term}} against the Mento Reserve mix. Pharos already tracks a larger ZAR issuer, so ZARm is mainly an ecosystem-completion row that lets users compare Mento's local-currency model across regions. The token passes the DefiLlama price and supply gate and uses the verified Celo contract. Reserve quality is inherited from the shared Mento reserve mix rather than from rand-denominated bank collateral, so {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk is on the Mento basket, not the South African banking system.

wbrl-ripio.title: Ripio's Wrapped Brazilian Real
wbrl-ripio.text: WBRL is Ripio's wrapped Brazilian real stablecoin across six EVM chains — a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer, with reserve transparency as the weak point. WBRL is part of Ripio's wFIAT suite: local-currency stablecoins issued across Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis. It passes DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply gate and gives Pharos a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer, alongside larger BRL assets already tracked.
